# Compliance Audit Log starter

A small, disposable starter for a local compliance audit-log service. The run
prompts grow it into a working service while preserving a stable CLI:

```text
python -m auditlog.cli record ACTOR ACTION OUTCOME --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli query --actor ACTOR --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli repair --log-store STORE.db
```

The trail is append-only. An entry, once recorded, is never removed, rewritten,
or reordered: corrections are made by recording a further entry, not by editing
history. Each entry carries a gapless `sequence` and an `event_id` derived
deterministically from the entry's own recorded content, so the same content
always yields the same id and any later edit is detectable by recomputing it.

Two log-store formats exist. The current format records each entry with an
explicit content-derived `event_id`. The older archive format used its own
`origin_ref` per entry and stored an export-observed `at` value rather than the
canonical recording time. It could renumber ids and restamp an event between
exports, so overlapping archive batches sometimes contain the same underlying
event twice with slightly different `at` values. Reading that format therefore
requires deciding when two archived entries are the same event and choosing one
representative timestamp deterministically.

`metadata` is caller-supplied descriptive context. It is never an input to an
entry's identity, and never an input to whether an entry is retained.

HTTP routing keeps request-path matching in `auditlog.paths` so
authentication and dispatch share one helper. V2 paths are aliases of
canonical V1 routes; resolving one through `auditlog.httpd` never yields a
weaker bearer requirement than its V1 route has. Client version selection
picks which path is called, never whether the call needs a bearer credential:
an alias with no declared requirement inherits the V1 route's (defaulting to
required if the V1 route is unknown), and an alias with an explicit
requirement is still floored by the V1 route, so a stale or mis-declared
catalog entry cannot open an unauthenticated path onto data V1 protects.

`record`, `query`, and `repair` are written only against the storage-independent
`LogStore` contract in `auditlog.service` (`read_only`, `load()`, `save()`), so a
new log-store format is added by writing one class that satisfies the
contract, not by teaching those functions a new branch. `SqliteLogStore` is
that proof: a brand-new `--log-store STORE.db` path becomes a durable SQLite
file, where every write commits as its own transaction, so a record made by
one process is durably visible to a query made by a separate process. The
JSON current and archive formats remain readable (and, for the archive,
migratable via `repair`) through the same `open_store` detection, based on
each file's own content, never its name.

`auditlog.httpd` also runs the one thing actually served over HTTP:
bearer-protected V1 routes (`POST /v1/entries`, `GET /v1/entries`, `GET
/v1/integrity`) backed by the same `LogStore` contract. `resolve_v1_route` is
the single lookup both the auth check and the dispatch use, so there is one
route decision, not two. The V2 alias catalog in `auditlog.policy` and its
resolution in `auditlog.httpd` are tested but not installed into that
server; nothing in the live route table references them. `auditlog.sdk_client`
is a small generated V1 client, one method per route, that always sends the
bearer credential those routes require.

`fixtures/sdk-request-response-fixtures.json` pins the exact request shape
(method, path, bearer header placement, body/query keys) and response shape
(exact key list, in order) for `record`, `query`, and `integrity`.
`tests/test_sdk_fixtures.py` checks the generated client against it two ways:
offline, by capturing the `Request` `AuditV1Client` builds without any network
call, and live, by running a real V1 server and checking response shape,
byte-for-byte JSON stability across repeated calls on unchanged state, and
that only the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header authenticates — a token
in the query string, the request body, or a header missing the `Bearer`
prefix is refused.

`auditlog.migration_diagnostics` compares the V1 calls the generated SDK
client actually issues against the planned V2 catalog (`auditlog.policy`)
entirely offline: `diagnose_migration` is pure data over data (no I/O), so
this comparison never sends V2 traffic — there is nothing to send it to, since
`create_server` never installs a V2 route. `capture_v1_calls` is the one
function that performs I/O, and it only drives the generated V1 client
against a live server to record what it actually sends; the recorded shape is
also pinned in `fixtures/v1-generated-calls.jsonl`. Runtime routing is
unchanged by any of this: the diagnostics module only reads
`auditlog.httpd.V1_ROUTES` and `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`, never installs
anything.

`auditlog.migration_reference` renders `docs/sdk-migration-reference.md`
from the compatibility catalog (`auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog`):
one Markdown row per stored catalog row, in the catalog's own order,
preserving each row's method, path, permission, and bearer requirement
exactly (an unset requirement is rendered as unset, never coerced to a
guessed boolean). A second row addressing a (method, path) pair already
seen is rejected rather than silently rendered. Rendering is pure and
offline — it never sends a request or touches what `auditlog.httpd`
serves — and rendering the same catalog twice always produces the same
text; `tests/test_migration_reference.py` checks the committed doc still
matches what the catalog renders today.

The project must remain local-only and use the Python standard library. Tests use
`unittest`, so the environment needs no dependency installation.

- **`auditlog/migration_checkpoint.py`** — `CheckpointStore`, a SQLite-backed, restart-safe store that persists only an opaque `call_id` and a `pending`/`completed` status per call — nothing about payload, response, or bearer token. - **`README.md`** updated to document both modules.

No existing product code, routes, or server behavior was modified — only new additive modules and their tests.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent

The project began as a standard-library Python audit service for an SDK migration and now includes a completed restart-safe migration replay layer.

Earlier completed product work:
- Preserve CLI commands `record`, `query`, and `repair`, required `--log-store` options, and `auditlog.cli.build_parser()`.
- Use immutable audit events with content-derived IDs, gapless sequences, storage-independent service APIs, JSON/archive compatibility, durable SQLite storage, bearer-protected V1 HTTP routes, a generated V1 SDK client, an offline V2 alias catalog, fixtures, migration diagnostics, and deterministic migration reference documentation.
- Keep V2 routes uninstalled and never send V2 traffic.
- Perform separate maintenance reviews for multiple evidence directories, with discovery-before-analysis, complete reads, file type, line count, SHA-256, source-backed comparisons, and isolated reports.

Most recent active request:
- Add restart-safe SDK migration checkpoints and idempotent replay of generated client calls.
- Persist only opaque call IDs and completion status.
- Never persist bearer tokens.
- Keep audit records immutable.
- Test crash recovery, duplicate replies, conflict handling, and separate-process continuation.

The implementation was completed. The initial duplicate-reply test exposed an important limitation: because V1 record identity includes the server-stamped receipt timestamp, a retry cannot always be deduplicated from content alone. The replay API was extended with an in-memory `already_applied` callback so callers can check whether a logical call already took effect before reissuing it. The corrected new tests and the full suite pass.

2. Key Technical Concepts

Project constraints:
- Python standard library only; no dependency installation.
- Local-only project.
- Tests use `unittest`.
- The environment previously reported Python 3.9.6.
- Existing V1 HTTP behavior and routes must remain unchanged.

Audit model:
- `AuditEvent` is a frozen dataclass.
- Identity fields are exactly `actor`, `action`, `outcome`, and `recorded_at`.
- `content_digest()` computes SHA-256 over those fields joined with `"\x1f"`.
- Metadata, source version, and archive-origin references are descriptive and do not affect identity.
- Audit history is append-only and immutable; corrections require new entries.
- Sequences must be exactly `1..N`.
- Integrity errors and sequence errors are separate.
- Integrity failures must not be silently repaired by recomputing IDs.

Storage:
- `LogStore` exposes `read_only`, `load()`, `save()`, and `repair()`.
- New paths default to SQLite.
- Existing stores are detected by content: SQLite magic header or JSON `store_version` 1/2.
- SQLite uses an `entries` table and transaction-backed writes.
- Archive stores are read-only for recording and migrate through `repair`.
- Repeating identical content with the same recorded timestamp is idempotent at the audit-service level.

HTTP/SDK:
- Runtime serves only:
  - `POST /v1/entries`
  - `GET /v1/entries`
  - `GET /v1/integrity`
- Every V1 route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Query parameters, request bodies, and authorization values without the `Bearer` prefix do not authenticate.
- Missing or invalid credentials return HTTP 401.
- Unknown/uninstalled V2 paths return HTTP 404.
- Authentication and dispatch reuse one route decision.
- `AuditV1Client` uses `urllib.request` and only addresses V1 routes.
- Migration diagnostics compare generated V1 calls with planned V2 aliases without sending V2 requests.

Checkpoint storage:
- `auditlog.migration_checkpoint.CheckpointStore` uses SQLite.
- Schema is exactly two application columns:
  `checkpoints(call_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL)`
- Status values are `pending` and `completed`.
- It persists only the caller-provided opaque `call_id` and status.
- It does not accept or store a bearer-token field, request payload, response, fingerprint, or callback.
- Each status update runs in its own SQLite transaction and is visible to a newly opened process using the same file.
- The API relies on the caller supplying a genuinely opaque, non-secret ID. It does not independently detect or reject a secret if a caller mistakenly passes one as `call_id`; tests verify that normal replay usage does not write the bearer token.

Replay:
- `ReplayCall` contains a call ID, an in-memory fingerprint, an invocation callback, and an optional `already_applied` callback.
- Fingerprints are never persisted.
- A reused ID with different fingerprints in one batch raises `ReplayConflictError`.
- A completed call is skipped without invoking it.
- For an incomplete call:
  - If `already_applied` exists and returns true, the call is marked completed and not invoked.
  - Otherwise it is marked pending, invoked, and marked completed only after successful return.
- A crash or exception during invocation leaves the call pending and retryable.
- The replay layer never mutates or deletes audit records.
- The `already_applied` hook is necessary for uncertain outcomes where a server-side call succeeded before the client crashed before writing its checkpoint. For V1 records, the server receipt timestamp is part of identity, so merely retrying the same actor/action/outcome may create a distinct event unless the caller independently confirms prior application.

3. Files and Code

Latest files created or changed:
- `auditlog/migration_checkpoint.py`
- `auditlog/migration_replay.py`
- `tests/test_migration_checkpoint.py`
- `tests/test_migration_replay.py`
- `README.md`

Important checkpoint code:
- Constants:
  `PENDING = "pending"`
  `COMPLETED = "completed"`
- Class:
  `CheckpointStore(path: Path)`
- Methods:
  - `status(call_id: str) -> str | None`
  - `is_completed(call_id: str) -> bool`
  - `mark_pending(call_id: str) -> None`
  - `mark_completed(call_id: str) -> None`
- SQLite writes use:
  `DELETE FROM checkpoints WHERE call_id = ?`
  followed by
  `INSERT INTO checkpoints (call_id, status) VALUES (?, ?)`
  inside a transaction.

Important replay code:
- `class ReplayConflictError(ValueError)`
- Frozen dataclass:
  `ReplayCall(call_id: str, fingerprint: str, invoke: Callable[[], object], already_applied: Callable[[], bool] | None = None)`
- Frozen dataclass:
  `ReplayOutcome(call_id: str, skipped: bool, result: object | None)`
- Function:
  `replay(calls: tuple[ReplayCall, ...], checkpoint: CheckpointStore) -> tuple[ReplayOutcome, ...]`

Core replay behavior:
- Tracks fingerprints in an in-memory dictionary.
- Raises `ReplayConflictError` when the same ID is used for differing fingerprints.

"""The host transport: bearer-protected V1 routes, and the V2 alias seam.

Two independent things live here. ``resolve_v2_alias_catalog`` is a stable,
offline resolution seam for compatibility work: given a V2 alias catalog and
the canonical V1 routes' bearer requirements, it computes what each alias's
effective requirement would be. It is not installed anywhere below — no
route table in this module references ``auditlog.policy`` or the V2 catalog.
The V1 HTTP server below is the only thing actually served, and it serves V1
paths exclusively.

A client selects a V2 alias by which path it calls, never by which bearer
requirement applies to that call: the resolved requirement can only ever be
at least as strict as the alias's canonical V1 route, never weaker. An alias
left unset (``requires_auth is None``) inherits the canonical route's
requirement, defaulting to required when the canonical route itself is
unknown. An alias that declares its requirement explicitly is still floored
by the canonical route, so a stale or mis-declared catalog entry (or a
client that negotiates an older SDK version) cannot open an unauthenticated
path onto data the V1 route protects.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import http.server
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs

from .paths import auth_path
from .service import (
    IntegrityError,
    LogStore,
    LogStoreError,
    SequenceError,
    open_store,
    query_events,
    record_event,
)
from .timeutil import now_utc


def resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...], canonical_bearer: dict[tuple[str, str], bool]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool], ...]:
    """Resolve inherited aliases through their canonical V1 route keys.

    The result is the canonical V1 route's requirement OR'd with whatever the
    alias entry declares, so version selection can add a bearer requirement
    but never remove one.
    """

    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]] = []
    for method, path, permission, requires_auth in catalog:
        canonical_path = path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1)
        canonical_requires_auth = canonical_bearer.get((method, canonical_path), True)
        effective_requires_auth = canonical_requires_auth or bool(requires_auth)
        resolved.append((method, path, permission, effective_requires_auth))
    return tuple(resolved)


# --- Bearer-protected V1 routes: the only routes actually served -----------

V1_ROUTES: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, bool]] = {
    ("POST", "/v1/entries"): ("record", True),
    ("GET", "/v1/entries"): ("query", True),
    ("GET", "/v1/integrity"): ("integrity", True),
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RouteDecision:
    permission: str
    requires_auth: bool


def resolve_v1_route(method: str, raw_path: str) -> RouteDecision | None:
    """The one lookup the auth check and the dispatch both use.

    ``auth_path`` is the same helper ``dispatch_path`` wraps (see
    ``auditlog.paths``), so there is exactly one canonical spelling of the
    request path in play. This function turns that one spelling into one
    route decision, and the handler below reuses it for both the auth check
    and the dispatch instead of resolving the route twice.
    """

    path_only, _, _ = raw_path.partition("?")
    path = auth_path(path_only)
    entry = V1_ROUTES.get((method, path))
    if entry is None:
        return None
    permission, requires_auth = entry
    return RouteDecision(permission=permission, requires_auth=requires_auth)


class AuditHTTPServer(http.server.HTTPServer):
    """An ``HTTPServer`` carrying the one log store and bearer token it serves."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        server_address: tuple[str, int],
        handler_class: type[http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler],
        *,
        store: LogStore,
        bearer_token: str,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(server_address, handler_class)
        self.store = store
        self.bearer_token = bearer_token


class V1RequestHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Serves the bearer-protected V1 routes; refuses anything else."""

    server: AuditHTTPServer

    def _authorized(self) -> bool:
        return self.headers.get("Authorization") == f"Bearer {self.server.bearer_token}"

    def _write_json(self, status: int, payload: object) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _handle(self, method: str) -> None:
        decision = resolve_v1_route(method, self.path)
        if decision is None:
            self._write_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
            return
        if decision.requires_auth and not self._authorized():
            self._write_json(401, {"error": "bearer credential required"})
            return
        try:
            self._dispatch(decision.permission)
        except (LogStoreError, IntegrityError, SequenceError) as exc:
            self._write_json(409, {"error": str(exc)})

    def _dispatch(self, permission: str) -> None:
        _, _, query_string = self.path.partition("?")
        if permission == "record":
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
            event = record_event(
                self.server.store,
                actor=body["actor"],
                action=body["action"],
                outcome=body["outcome"],
                recorded_at=now_utc(),
                metadata=body.get("metadata", {}),
            )
            self._write_json(200, event.to_record())
        elif permission == "query":
            params = parse_qs(query_string)
            events = query_events(
                self.server.store,
                actor=(params.get("actor") or [None])[0],
                action=(params.get("action") or [None])[0],
            )
            self._write_json(200, [event.to_record() for event in events])
        else:  # "integrity"
            events = self.server.store.load()
            self._write_json(200, {"ok": True, "event_count": len(events)})

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        self._handle("POST")

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        self._handle("GET")

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:  # quiet during tests
        pass


def create_server(
    log_store_path: Path, bearer_token: str, *, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 0
) -> AuditHTTPServer:
    """Build the V1-only server. The V2 alias catalog is not installed here."""

    store = open_store(log_store_path)
    return AuditHTTPServer((host, port), V1RequestHandler, store=store, bearer_token=bearer_token)

"""Command-line shell for the audit log service.

Each command is a thin adapter onto ``auditlog.service``: the CLI parses
arguments and formats output, and the service functions carry all of the
storage-independent behavior (identity, sequencing, integrity, repair).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from .service import LogStoreError, open_store, query_events, record_event
from .timeutil import now_utc


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Return the stable top-level parser the acceptance path imports.

    The ``record``/``query``/``repair`` commands and their required
    ``--log-store`` option are the documented contract; keep them.
    """

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="auditlog")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    record = subparsers.add_parser("record", help="append an entry to the trail")
    record.add_argument("actor")
    record.add_argument("action")
    record.add_argument("outcome")
    record.add_argument(
        "--metadata",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="KEY=VALUE",
        help="descriptive context to store with the entry; repeatable",
    )
    record.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    query = subparsers.add_parser("query", help="read entries from the trail")
    query.add_argument("--actor")
    query.add_argument("--action")
    query.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    repair = subparsers.add_parser("repair", help="rebuild derived indexes")
    repair.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)
    return parser


def _parse_metadata(pairs: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Turn repeated ``KEY=VALUE`` options into the metadata dict callers see."""

    metadata: dict[str, str] = {}
    for pair in pairs:
        key, sep, value = pair.partition("=")
        if not sep:
            raise ValueError(f"--metadata expects KEY=VALUE, got {pair!r}")
        metadata[key] = value
    return metadata


def _run_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    event = record_event(
        store,
        actor=args.actor,
        action=args.action,
        outcome=args.outcome,
        recorded_at=now_utc(),
        metadata=_parse_metadata(args.metadata),
    )
    print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_query(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    for event in query_events(store, actor=args.actor, action=args.action):
        print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_repair(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    report = store.repair()
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "event_count": report.event_count,
                "resequenced": report.resequenced,
                "migrated_from_archive": report.migrated_from_archive,
            }
        )
    )
    return 0


_HANDLERS = {"record": _run_record, "query": _run_query, "repair": _run_repair}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse the command line and dispatch to the matching command handler."""

    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return _HANDLERS[args.command](args)
    except (LogStoreError, ValueError) as exc:
        parser.error(str(exc))
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""Storage-independent audit-log service contract.
2	
3	``record_event`` and ``query_events`` are written only against the
4	``LogStore`` protocol below: ``read_only``, ``load()``, ``save()``. Neither
5	function knows or cares whether the bytes on disk are the current format or
6	the legacy archive format. ``repair()`` is the one operation each store
7	implements itself, because "rebuild the derived index" means something
8	different per format: resequence-and-verify for the current format, migrate
9	for the archive format.
10	
11	This is what "storage-independent" buys: a new log-store format is added by
12	writing one class that satisfies the protocol, not by teaching `record`,
13	`query`, or the CLI a new branch. ``SqliteLogStore`` is the proof: a durable,
14	cross-process-safe format that ``record_event`` and ``query_events`` use
15	exactly as they use the JSON-backed ``CurrentLogStore``.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import json
21	import sqlite3
22	from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
23	from pathlib import Path
24	from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
25	
26	from .models import AuditEvent, content_digest
27	from .timeutil import canonical_timestamp
28	
29	
30	class LogStoreError(Exception):
31	    """Base for problems reading or writing a log store."""
32	
33	
34	class IntegrityError(LogStoreError):
35	    """A stored entry's content no longer matches its recorded event_id.
36	
37	    This is never auto-corrected: recomputing a new id for tampered content
38	    would erase the only evidence that the trail was altered.
39	    """
40	
41	
42	class SequenceError(LogStoreError):
43	    """The stored sequence is not the gapless ``1..N`` the trail requires."""
44	
45	
46	@runtime_checkable
47	class LogStore(Protocol):
48	    """Contract every log-store format must satisfy.
49	
50	    ``read_only`` marks formats (the archive) that cannot accept new
51	    entries directly; callers must repair them into the current format
52	    first.
53	    """
54	
55	    read_only: bool
56	
57	    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
58	        """Return every event in the trail, in gapless sequence order."""
59	        ...
60	
61	    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
62	        """Persist exactly this list of events as the entire trail."""
63	        ...
64	
65	    def repair(self) -> "RepairReport":
66	        """Rebuild this store's derived index; return a summary of what changed."""
67	        ...
68	
69	
70	@dataclass(frozen=True)
71	class RepairReport:
72	    event_count: int
73	    resequenced: bool
74	    migrated_from_archive: bool
75	
76	
77	def _verify_integrity(events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
78	    tampered = [event for event in events if event.event_id != event.recomputed_id()]
79	    if tampered:
80	        bad_ids = ", ".join(event.event_id for event in tampered)
81	        raise IntegrityError(
82	            f"recorded content no longer matches the stored event_id for: {bad_ids}"
83	        )
84	
85	
86	def _verify_gapless(events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
87	    expected = list(range(1, len(events) + 1))
88	    actual = [event.sequence for event in events]
89	    if actual != expected:
90	        raise SequenceError(f"sequence is not gapless 1..{len(events)}: got {actual}")
91	
92	
93	class CurrentLogStore:
94	    """The current log-store format (store_version 2): explicit content-derived ids."""
95	
96	    read_only = False
97	
98	    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
99	        self.path = path
100	
101	    def _read_raw(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
102	        if not self.path.exists() or self.path.stat().st_size == 0:
103	            return []
104	        raw = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
105	        return [AuditEvent.from_current_record(record) for record in raw.get("entries", [])]
106	
107	    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
108	        events = self._read_raw()
109	        _verify_integrity(events)
110	        _verify_gapless(events)
111	        return events
112	
113	    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
114	        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
115	            "store_version": 2,
116	            "entries": [event.to_record() for event in events],
117	        }
118	        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
119	
120	    def repair(self) -> RepairReport:
121	        events = self._read_raw()
122	        _verify_integrity(events)
123	        resequenced_events = [
124	            replace(event, sequence=index) for index, event in enumerate(events, start=1)
125	        ]
126	        changed = [event.sequence for event in events] != [
127	            event.sequence for event in resequenced_events
128	        ]
129	        self.save(resequenced_events)
130	        return RepairReport(
131	            event_count=len(resequenced_events),
132	            resequenced=changed,
133	            migrated_from_archive=False,
134	        )
135	
136	
137	class ArchiveLogStore:
138	    """The older archive format (store_version 1): read-only, export-time-stamped.
139	
140	    Overlapping export batches can contain the same underlying event twice
141	    under different ``ref``s and ``at`` values, so loading requires grouping
142	    entries into events and picking one deterministic representative
143	    timestamp per group. The earliest observed ``at`` is used, since it is
144	    the export closest to the event's actual occurrence.
145	    """
146	
147	    read_only = True
148	
149	    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
150	        self.path = path
151	
152	    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
153	        raw = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
154	        groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
155	        for entry in raw.get("entries", []):
156	            key = (entry["actor"], entry["action"], entry["outcome"])
157	            groups.setdefault(key, []).append(entry)
158	
159	        canonical: list[tuple[str, str, str, str, list[str]]] = []
160	        for (actor, action, outcome), entries in groups.items():
161	            recorded_at = min(canonical_timestamp(entry["at"]) for entry in entries)
162	            origin_refs = sorted(entry["ref"] for entry in entries)
163	            canonical.append((recorded_at, actor, action, outcome, origin_refs))
164	        canonical.sort(key=lambda item: item[:4])
165	
166	        return [
167	            AuditEvent.from_archive_group(
168	                actor=actor,
169	                action=action,
170	                outcome=outcome,
171	                recorded_at=recorded_at,
172	                sequence=sequence,
173	                origin_refs=origin_refs,
174	            )
175	            for sequence, (recorded_at, actor, action, outcome, origin_refs) in enumerate(
176	                canonical, start=1
177	            )
178	        ]
179	
180	    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
181	        raise LogStoreError(
182	            "archive-format stores are read-only; run `repair` to migrate to the current format"
183	        )
184	
185	    def repair(self) -> RepairReport:
186	        events = self.load()
187	        CurrentLogStore(self.path).save(events)
188	        return RepairReport(event_count=len(events), resequenced=True, migrated_from_archive=True)
189	
190	
191	_SQLITE_MAGIC = b"SQLite format 3\x00"
192	
193	
194	class SqliteLogStore:
195	    """A durable log-store format backed by SQLite.
196	
197	    Every write commits as its own SQLite transaction, so a record made by
198	    one process is durable and immediately visible to a query made by a
199	    separate process against the same file. A plain JSON-file rewrite offers
200	    no such guarantee, which is why this, not the current-format JSON file,
201	    is what a brand-new ``--log-store`` path becomes.
202	    """
203	
204	    read_only = False
205	
206	    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
207	        self.path = path
208	
209	    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
210	        connection = sqlite3.connect(self.path)
211	        connection.execute(
212	            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries ("
213	            "sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "
214	            "event_id TEXT NOT NULL, "
215	            "actor TEXT NOT NULL, "
216	            "action TEXT NOT NULL, "
217	            "outcome TEXT NOT NULL, "
218	            "recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL, "
219	            "metadata TEXT NOT NULL)"
220	        )
221	        connection.commit()
222	        return connection
223	
224	    @staticmethod
225	    def _row_to_event(row: tuple[Any, ...]) -> AuditEvent:
226	        sequence, event_id, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, metadata = row
227	        return AuditEvent(
228	            event_id=event_id,
229	            sequence=sequence,
230	            actor=actor,
231	            action=action,
232	            outcome=outcome,
233	            recorded_at=recorded_at,
234	            metadata=json.loads(metadata),
235	        )
236	
237	    def _read_raw(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
238	        connection = self._connect()
239	        try:
240	            rows = connection.execute(
241	                "SELECT sequence, event_id, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, metadata "
242	                "FROM entries ORDER BY sequence"
243	            ).fetchall()
244	        finally:
245	            connection.close()
246	        return [self._row_to_event(row) for row in rows]
247	
248	    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
249	        events = self._read_raw()
250	        _verify_integrity(events)
251	        _verify_gapless(events)
252	        return events
253	
254	    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
255	        connection = self._connect()
256	        try:
257	            with connection:
258	                connection.execute("DELETE FROM entries")
259	                connection.executemany(
260	                    "INSERT INTO entries "
261	                    "(sequence, event_id, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, metadata) "
262	                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
263	                    [
264	                        (
265	                            event.sequence,
266	                            event.event_id,
267	                            event.actor,
268	                            event.action,
269	                            event.outcome,
270	                            event.recorded_at,
271	                            json.dumps(dict(event.metadata)),
272	                        )
273	                        for event in events
274	                    ],
275	                )
276	        finally:
277	            connection.close()
278	
279	    def repair(self) -> RepairReport:
280	        events = self._read_raw()
281	        _verify_integrity(events)
282	        resequenced_events = [
283	            replace(event, sequence=index) for index, event in enumerate(events, start=1)
284	        ]
285	        changed = [event.sequence for event in events] != [
286	            event.sequence for event in resequenced_events
287	        ]
288	        self.save(resequenced_events)
289	        return RepairReport(
290	            event_count=len(resequenced_events),
291	            resequenced=changed,
292	            migrated_from_archive=False,
293	        )
294	
295	
296	def open_store(path: Path) -> LogStore:
297	    """Detect a log-store's format from its content and return the matching store.
298	
299	    A path that does not exist yet (or is empty) is a brand-new store: it
300	    becomes the durable SQLite format, matching the ``--log-store STORE.db``
301	    naming the CLI has always documented. An existing file is identified by
302	    its own content — the SQLite header, or a JSON ``store_version`` — never
303	    by its name.
304	    """
305	
306	    if not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size == 0:
307	        return SqliteLogStore(path)
308	    with path.open("rb") as handle:
309	        header = handle.read(len(_SQLITE_MAGIC))
310	    if header == _SQLITE_MAGIC:
311	        return SqliteLogStore(path)
312	    try:
313	        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
314	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
315	        raise LogStoreError(f"{path} is neither a SQLite file nor valid JSON") from exc
316	    version = raw.get("store_version")
317	    if version == 1:
318	        return ArchiveLogStore(path)
319	    if version == 2:
320	        return CurrentLogStore(path)
321	    raise LogStoreError(f"{path} has unknown store_version {version!r}")
322	
323	
324	def record_event(
325	    store: LogStore,
326	    *,
327	    actor: str,
328	    action: str,
329	    outcome: str,
330	    recorded_at: str,
331	    metadata: dict[str, Any],
332	) -> AuditEvent:
333	    """Append one entry; identical content submitted again returns the existing entry.
334	
335	    Identity is the recorded content, so recording the same (actor, action,
336	    outcome, recorded_at) twice must collapse to the one event it always
337	    was, not create a second trail entry.
338	    """
339	
340	    if store.read_only:
341	        raise LogStoreError(
342	            "cannot record into an archive-format store; run `repair` to migrate it first"
343	        )
344	    events = store.load()
345	    event_id = content_digest(actor, action, outcome, recorded_at)
346	    for existing in events:
347	        if existing.event_id == event_id:
348	            return existing
349	    event = AuditEvent(
350	        event_id=event_id,
351	        sequence=len(events) + 1,
352	        actor=actor,

"""Storage-independent audit-log service contract.

``record_event`` and ``query_events`` are written only against the
``LogStore`` protocol below: ``read_only``, ``load()``, ``save()``. Neither
function knows or cares whether the bytes on disk are the current format or
the legacy archive format. ``repair()`` is the one operation each store
implements itself, because "rebuild the derived index" means something
different per format: resequence-and-verify for the current format, migrate
for the archive format.

This is what "storage-independent" buys: a new log-store format is added by
writing one class that satisfies the protocol, not by teaching `record`,
`query`, or the CLI a new branch. ``SqliteLogStore`` is the proof: a durable,
cross-process-safe format that ``record_event`` and ``query_events`` use
exactly as they use the JSON-backed ``CurrentLogStore``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from .models import AuditEvent, content_digest
from .timeutil import canonical_timestamp


class LogStoreError(Exception):
    """Base for problems reading or writing a log store."""


class IntegrityError(LogStoreError):
    """A stored entry's content no longer matches its recorded event_id.

    This is never auto-corrected: recomputing a new id for tampered content
    would erase the only evidence that the trail was altered.
    """


class SequenceError(LogStoreError):
    """The stored sequence is not the gapless ``1..N`` the trail requires."""


@runtime_checkable
class LogStore(Protocol):
    """Contract every log-store format must satisfy.

    ``read_only`` marks formats (the archive) that cannot accept new
    entries directly; callers must repair them into the current format
    first.
    """

    read_only: bool

    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        """Return every event in the trail, in gapless sequence order."""
        ...

    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
        """Persist exactly this list of events as the entire trail."""
        ...

    def repair(self) -> "RepairReport":
        """Rebuild this store's derived index; return a summary of what changed."""
        ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RepairReport:
    event_count: int
    resequenced: bool
    migrated_from_archive: bool


def _verify_integrity(events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
    tampered = [event for event in events if event.event_id != event.recomputed_id()]
    if tampered:
        bad_ids = ", ".join(event.event_id for event in tampered)
        raise IntegrityError(
            f"recorded content no longer matches the stored event_id for: {bad_ids}"
        )


def _verify_gapless(events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
    expected = list(range(1, len(events) + 1))
    actual = [event.sequence for event in events]
    if actual != expected:
        raise SequenceError(f"sequence is not gapless 1..{len(events)}: got {actual}")


class CurrentLogStore:
    """The current log-store format (store_version 2): explicit content-derived ids."""

    read_only = False

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = path

    def _read_raw(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        if not self.path.exists() or self.path.stat().st_size == 0:
            return []
        raw = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return [AuditEvent.from_current_record(record) for record in raw.get("entries", [])]

    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        events = self._read_raw()
        _verify_integrity(events)
        _verify_gapless(events)
        return events

    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "store_version": 2,
            "entries": [event.to_record() for event in events],
        }
        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    def repair(self) -> RepairReport:
        events = self._read_raw()
        _verify_integrity(events)
        resequenced_events = [
            replace(event, sequence=index) for index, event in enumerate(events, start=1)
        ]
        changed = [event.sequence for event in events] != [
            event.sequence for event in resequenced_events
        ]
        self.save(resequenced_events)
        return RepairReport(
            event_count=len(resequenced_events),
            resequenced=changed,
            migrated_from_archive=False,
        )


class ArchiveLogStore:
    """The older archive format (store_version 1): read-only, export-time-stamped.

    Overlapping export batches can contain the same underlying event twice
    under different ``ref``s and ``at`` values, so loading requires grouping
    entries into events and picking one deterministic representative
    timestamp per group. The earliest observed ``at`` is used, since it is
    the export closest to the event's actual occurrence.
    """

    read_only = True

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = path

    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        raw = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        for entry in raw.get("entries", []):
            key = (entry["actor"], entry["action"], entry["outcome"])
            groups.setdefault(key, []).append(entry)

        canonical: list[tuple[str, str, str, str, list[str]]] = []
        for (actor, action, outcome), entries in groups.items():
            recorded_at = min(canonical_timestamp(entry["at"]) for entry in entries)
            origin_refs = sorted(entry["ref"] for entry in entries)
            canonical.append((recorded_at, actor, action, outcome, origin_refs))
        canonical.sort(key=lambda item: item[:4])

        return [
            AuditEvent.from_archive_group(
                actor=actor,
                action=action,
                outcome=outcome,
                recorded_at=recorded_at,
                sequence=sequence,
                origin_refs=origin_refs,
            )
            for sequence, (recorded_at, actor, action, outcome, origin_refs) in enumerate(
                canonical, start=1
            )
        ]

    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
        raise LogStoreError(
            "archive-format stores are read-only; run `repair` to migrate to the current format"
        )

    def repair(self) -> RepairReport:
        events = self.load()
        CurrentLogStore(self.path).save(events)
        return RepairReport(event_count=len(events), resequenced=True, migrated_from_archive=True)


_SQLITE_MAGIC = b"SQLite format 3\x00"


class SqliteLogStore:
    """A durable log-store format backed by SQLite.

    Every write commits as its own SQLite transaction, so a record made by
    one process is durable and immediately visible to a query made by a
    separate process against the same file. A plain JSON-file rewrite offers
    no such guarantee, which is why this, not the current-format JSON file,
    is what a brand-new ``--log-store`` path becomes.
    """

    read_only = False

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = path

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        connection = sqlite3.connect(self.path)
        connection.execute(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries ("
            "sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, "
            "event_id TEXT NOT NULL, "
            "actor TEXT NOT NULL, "
            "action TEXT NOT NULL, "
            "outcome TEXT NOT NULL, "
            "recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL, "
            "metadata TEXT NOT NULL)"
        )
        connection.commit()
        return connection

    @staticmethod
    def _row_to_event(row: tuple[Any, ...]) -> AuditEvent:
        sequence, event_id, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, metadata = row
        return AuditEvent(
            event_id=event_id,
            sequence=sequence,
            actor=actor,
            action=action,
            outcome=outcome,
            recorded_at=recorded_at,
            metadata=json.loads(metadata),
        )

    def _read_raw(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        connection = self._connect()
        try:
            rows = connection.execute(
                "SELECT sequence, event_id, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, metadata "
                "FROM entries ORDER BY sequence"
            ).fetchall()
        finally:
            connection.close()
        return [self._row_to_event(row) for row in rows]

    def load(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        events = self._read_raw()
        _verify_integrity(events)
        _verify_gapless(events)
        return events

    def save(self, events: list[AuditEvent]) -> None:
        connection = self._connect()
        try:
            with connection:
                connection.execute("DELETE FROM entries")
                connection.executemany(
                    "INSERT INTO entries "
                    "(sequence, event_id, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, metadata) "
                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    [
                        (
                            event.sequence,
                            event.event_id,
                            event.actor,
                            event.action,
                            event.outcome,
                            event.recorded_at,
                            json.dumps(dict(event.metadata)),
                        )
                        for event in events
                    ],
                )
        finally:
            connection.close()

    def repair(self) -> RepairReport:
        events = self._read_raw()
        _verify_integrity(events)
        resequenced_events = [
            replace(event, sequence=index) for index, event in enumerate(events, start=1)
        ]
        changed = [event.sequence for event in events] != [
            event.sequence for event in resequenced_events
        ]
        self.save(resequenced_events)
        return RepairReport(
            event_count=len(resequenced_events),
            resequenced=changed,
            migrated_from_archive=False,
        )


def open_store(path: Path) -> LogStore:
    """Detect a log-store's format from its content and return the matching store.

    A path that does not exist yet (or is empty) is a brand-new store: it
    becomes the durable SQLite format, matching the ``--log-store STORE.db``
    naming the CLI has always documented. An existing file is identified by
    its own content — the SQLite header, or a JSON ``store_version`` — never
    by its name.
    """

    if not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size == 0:
        return SqliteLogStore(path)
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        header = handle.read(len(_SQLITE_MAGIC))
    if header == _SQLITE_MAGIC:
        return SqliteLogStore(path)
    try:
        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise LogStoreError(f"{path} is neither a SQLite file nor valid JSON") from exc
    version = raw.get("store_version")
    if version == 1:
        return ArchiveLogStore(path)
    if version == 2:
        return CurrentLogStore(path)
    raise LogStoreError(f"{path} has unknown store_version {version!r}")


def record_event(
    store: LogStore,
    *,
    actor: str,
    action: str,
    outcome: str,
    recorded_at: str,
    metadata: dict[str, Any],
) -> AuditEvent:
    """Append one entry; identical content submitted again returns the existing entry.

    Identity is the recorded content, so recording the same (actor, action,
    outcome, recorded_at) twice must collapse to the one event it always
    was, not create a second trail entry.
    """

    if store.read_only:
        raise LogStoreError(
            "cannot record into an archive-format store; run `repair` to migrate it first"
        )
    events = store.load()
    event_id = content_digest(actor, action, outcome, recorded_at)
    for existing in events:
        if existing.event_id == event_id:
            return existing
    event = AuditEvent(
        event_id=event_id,
        sequence=len(events) + 1,
        actor=actor,
        action=action,
        outcome=outcome,
        recorded_at=recorded_at,
        metadata=dict(metadata),
    )
    store.save(events + [event])
    return event


def query_events(
    store: LogStore, *, actor: str | None = None, action: str | None = None
) -> list[AuditEvent]:
    """Return trail entries matching every given filter."""

    events = store.load()
    if actor is not None:
        events = [event for event in events if event.actor == actor]
    if action is not None:
        events = [event for event in events if event.action == action]
    return events

"""HTTP-layer tests: the V2 catalog's fixed shape, and V1 bearer refusal.

The V1 server is the only thing actually served (``create_server`` never
installs the V2 alias catalog), so these tests run a real V1 server on a
loopback socket and drive it with real HTTP requests: no Authorization
header, the wrong bearer token, and — via the generated SDK client — the
correct one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import threading
import unittest
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from urllib.error import HTTPError

from auditlog.httpd import create_server
from auditlog.policy import build_v2_alias_catalog
from auditlog.sdk_client import AuditV1Client


class V2CatalogTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_catalog_returns_the_three_fixed_v2_rows_with_explicit_true(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            build_v2_alias_catalog(),
            (
                ("POST", "/v2/entries", "record", True),
                ("GET", "/v2/entries", "query", True),
                ("GET", "/v2/integrity", "integrity", True),
            ),
        )


class V1RouteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        store_path = Path(self._tmp.name) / "store.db"

        self.server = create_server(store_path, "s3cret", port=0)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._shutdown)
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"

    def _shutdown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.thread.join()
        self.server.server_close()

    def test_request_without_a_bearer_token_is_refused(self) -> None:
        request = urllib.request.Request(f"{self.base_url}/v1/entries", method="GET")
        with self.assertRaises(HTTPError) as ctx:
            urllib.request.urlopen(request)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, 401)

    def test_request_with_the_wrong_bearer_token_is_refused(self) -> None:
        client = AuditV1Client(self.base_url, bearer_token="wrong")
        with self.assertRaises(HTTPError) as ctx:
            client.query()
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, 401)

    def test_v2_paths_are_not_installed_on_the_v1_server(self) -> None:
        client = AuditV1Client(self.base_url, bearer_token="s3cret")
        with self.assertRaises(HTTPError) as ctx:
            client._request("GET", "/v2/entries")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, 404)

    def test_request_with_the_correct_bearer_token_is_served(self) -> None:
        client = AuditV1Client(self.base_url, bearer_token="s3cret")
        recorded = client.record("mina", "policy.update", "allowed")
        self.assertEqual(recorded["actor"], "mina")
        self.assertEqual(recorded["sequence"], 1)

        events = client.query(actor="mina")
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0]["event_id"], recorded["event_id"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

6	``diagnose_migration`` takes a record of V1 calls (however it was obtained)
7	and the planned V2 catalog (``auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog``) and
8	performs no I/O at all. ``capture_v1_calls`` is the one function here that
9	performs I/O, and it only ever drives the generated V1 SDK client
10	(``auditlog.sdk_client.AuditV1Client``), which itself only ever addresses
11	``/v1/...`` paths.

15	
16	import urllib.request
17	from dataclasses import dataclass
18	from urllib.parse import urlsplit
19	
20	from .httpd import V1_ROUTES, resolve_v2_alias_catalog
21	from .sdk_client import AuditV1Client

23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class GeneratedCall:
26	    """One call the generated SDK client issued, or is asserted to issue, against V1."""
27	
28	    method: str
29	    path: str
30	    used_bearer: bool
31	
32	
33	@dataclass(frozen=True)
34	class MigrationDiscrepancy:
35	    """One way a generated V1 call and the planned V2 catalog disagree."""
36	
37	    method: str
38	    v1_path: str
39	    v2_path: str | None
40	    reason: str

43	def diagnose_migration(
44	    generated_calls: tuple[GeneratedCall, ...],
45	    planned_v2_catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...],
46	) -> tuple[MigrationDiscrepancy, ...]:
47	    """Cross-check generated V1 calls against the planned V2 catalog, offline.
48	
49	    Every V2 alias is resolved through the same non-weakening logic
50	    (``resolve_v2_alias_catalog``) the live bearer-check invariant uses,
51	    floored by the real V1 route table (``V1_ROUTES``) rather than by data
52	    this function invents. No request of any kind is made here, so nothing
53	    below ever addresses a V2 path.
54	    """
55	
56	    canonical_bearer = {
57	        (method, path): requires_auth
58	        for (method, path), (_permission, requires_auth) in V1_ROUTES.items()
59	    }
60	    resolved_v2 = {
61	        (method, path): requires_auth
62	        for method, path, _permission, requires_auth in resolve_v2_alias_catalog(
63	            planned_v2_catalog, canonical_bearer
64	        )
65	    }
66	    planned_v1_paths = {
67	        (method, path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1))
68	        for method, path, _permission, _requires_auth in planned_v2_catalog
69	    }
70	
71	    discrepancies: list[MigrationDiscrepancy] = []
72	    covered_v1: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
73	
74	    for call in generated_calls:
75	        key = (call.method, call.path)
76	        covered_v1.add(key)
77	        if key not in planned_v1_paths:
78	            discrepancies.append(
79	                MigrationDiscrepancy(
80	                    call.method, call.path, None, "no planned V2 alias covers this V1 call"
81	                )
82	            )

85	        if resolved_v2.get((call.method, v2_path), True) and not call.used_bearer:
86	            discrepancies.append(
87	                MigrationDiscrepancy(
88	                    call.method,
89	                    call.path,
90	                    v2_path,
91	                    "generated call omitted the bearer credential its planned V2 alias requires",
92	                )
93	            )
94	
95	    for method, path in sorted(planned_v1_paths - covered_v1):
96	        v2_path = path.replace("/v1/", "/v2/", 1)
97	        discrepancies.append(
98	            MigrationDiscrepancy(

100	            )
101	        )

103	    return tuple(discrepancies)

107	    """Drive the generated SDK client against a live V1 server and record what it sent.
108

110	    makes rather than assuming it, so the result reflects the client's real
111	    behavior. The client itself only ever addresses ``/v1/...`` paths.
112	    """

114	    captured: list[GeneratedCall] = []
115	    real_urlopen = urllib.request.urlopen
116	
117	    def _capturing_urlopen(request: urllib.request.Request, *args: object, **kwargs: object) -> object:
118	        captured.append(
119	            GeneratedCall(
120	                method=request.get_method(),
121	                path=urlsplit(request.full_url).path,
122	                used_bearer=(request.get_header("Authorization") or "").startswith("Bearer "),
123	            )
124	        )
125	        return real_urlopen(request, *args, **kwargs)

133	    finally:
134	        urllib.request.urlopen = real_urlopen
135	
136	    return tuple(captured)

"""Render generated SDK migration reference material from the compatibility catalog.

Turn 3 built ``auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog`` as the stable,
offline compatibility catalog: one row per planned V2 alias, each carrying
its method, V2 path, permission, and bearer requirement. This module turns
that catalog into human-readable reference material without sending any
request or touching server behavior: ``render_migration_reference`` reads
the catalog's own tuples and writes them out; it never opens a socket, and
nothing here is installed into ``auditlog.httpd``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from .policy import build_v2_alias_catalog


class DuplicateCatalogRowError(ValueError):
    """Raised when two catalog rows address the same (method, path) route."""


def render_migration_reference(
    catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render the compatibility catalog as deterministic Markdown reference material.

    Every stored row is written out exactly as the catalog holds it — same
    method, same path, same permission label, same bearer requirement
    (including an unset ``None``, rendered as such rather than coerced to a
    guessed boolean) — in the exact order the catalog stores it, never
    resorted or grouped. A second row addressing a (method, path) pair
    already seen is rejected rather than silently rendered, so the
    reference material can never show two different entries for what is
    really one route. Calling this twice for the same catalog always
    produces the same string.
    """

    if catalog is None:
        catalog = build_v2_alias_catalog()

    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    rows: list[str] = []
    for method, path, permission, requires_auth in catalog:
        key = (method, path)
        if key in seen:
            raise DuplicateCatalogRowError(
                f"duplicate compatibility catalog row for {method} {path}"
            )
        seen.add(key)
        bearer_cell = "unset (inherits V1)" if requires_auth is None else str(requires_auth)
        rows.append(f"| {method} | {path} | {permission} | {bearer_cell} |")

    lines = [
        "# Generated SDK Migration Reference",
        "",
        "Generated from `auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog`. Offline",
        "reference material only: nothing here sends a request or changes",
        "what the V1 server serves.",
        "",
        "| Method | V2 Path | Permission | Bearer Required |",
        "|---|---|---|---|",
        *rows,
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

    ) -> None:

"""Strict SDK request/response fixtures for record, query, and integrity.

Two kinds of checks, both against ``fixtures/sdk-request-response-fixtures.json``:

* ``RequestShapeTests`` runs offline (no server, no network): it captures the
  actual ``urllib.request.Request`` the generated SDK client
  (``auditlog.sdk_client.AuditV1Client``) constructs and checks its method,
  path, bearer placement (the ``Authorization`` header, nothing else), and
  body/query keys against the fixture.
* ``ResponseShapeAndBearerPlacementTests`` runs a real V1 server and checks
  that responses carry exactly the fixture's declared keys in the fixture's
  order, that repeated calls against unchanged state are byte-identical
  JSON, and that only the ``Authorization: Bearer <token>`` header
  authenticates — a token anywhere else (query string, request body, header
  without the ``Bearer`` prefix) is refused.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

from auditlog.httpd import create_server
from auditlog.sdk_client import AuditV1Client

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures"


def _load_fixtures() -> dict:
    return json.loads((FIXTURES / "sdk-request-response-fixtures.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


class _FakeResponse:
    def __init__(self, body: bytes) -> None:
        self._body = body

    def __enter__(self) -> "_FakeResponse":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> bool:
        return False

    def read(self) -> bytes:
        return self._body


class RequestShapeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """What the client actually constructs, captured without any network call."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.fixtures = _load_fixtures()
        self.captured: list[urllib.request.Request] = []
        self._real_urlopen = urllib.request.urlopen
        urllib.request.urlopen = self._capture
        self.addCleanup(self._restore)
        self.client = AuditV1Client("http://example.invalid", bearer_token="tok-123")

    def _capture(self, request: urllib.request.Request, *args: object, **kwargs: object) -> _FakeResponse:
        self.captured.append(request)
        return _FakeResponse(b"{}")

    def _restore(self) -> None:
        urllib.request.urlopen = self._real_urlopen

    def _assert_matches_fixture(self, request: urllib.request.Request, fixture: dict) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(request.get_method(), fixture["method"])
        self.assertEqual(urlsplit(request.full_url).path, fixture["path"])
        self.assertEqual(request.get_header(fixture["bearer_header"]), "Bearer tok-123")

    def test_record_request_matches_the_fixture_method_path_and_bearer_placement(self) -> None:
        fixture = self.fixtures["record"]
        self.client.record("mina", "policy.update", "allowed", metadata={"k": "v"})
        request = self.captured[-1]
        self._assert_matches_fixture(request, fixture)
        body = json.loads(request.data.decode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(sorted(body.keys()), sorted(fixture["request_body_keys"]))

    def test_query_request_matches_the_fixture_method_path_and_bearer_placement(self) -> None:
        fixture = self.fixtures["query"]
        self.client.query(actor="mina", action="policy.update")
        request = self.captured[-1]
        self._assert_matches_fixture(request, fixture)
        sent_query_keys = sorted(parse_qs(urlsplit(request.full_url).query).keys())
        self.assertEqual(sent_query_keys, sorted(fixture["request_query_keys"]))

    def test_integrity_request_matches_the_fixture_method_path_and_bearer_placement(self) -> None:
        fixture = self.fixtures["integrity"]
        self.client.integrity()
        request = self.captured[-1]
        self._assert_matches_fixture(request, fixture)


class ResponseShapeAndBearerPlacementTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Real V1 server: response shape, JSON stability, and bearer placement."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.fixtures = _load_fixtures()
        self._tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        store_path = Path(self._tmp.name) / "store.db"
        self.server = create_server(store_path, "s3cret", port=0)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._shutdown)
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"
        self.client = AuditV1Client(self.base_url, bearer_token="s3cret")

    def _shutdown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.thread.join()
        self.server.server_close()

    def _raw(
        self, method: str, path: str, *, headers: dict | None = None, body: bytes | None = None
    ) -> bytes:
        request = urllib.request.Request(f"{self.base_url}{path}", data=body, method=method)
        for key, value in (headers or {}).items():
            request.add_header(key, value)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
            return response.read()

    def test_record_response_has_exactly_the_fixture_keys_in_order(self) -> None:
        fixture = self.fixtures["record"]
        recorded = self.client.record("mina", "policy.update", "allowed")
        self.assertEqual(list(recorded.keys()), fixture["response_keys"])

    def test_integrity_response_has_exactly_the_fixture_keys_in_order(self) -> None:
        fixture = self.fixtures["integrity"]
        result = self.client.integrity()
        self.assertEqual(list(result.keys()), fixture["response_keys"])

    def test_query_response_is_a_list_of_records_with_exactly_the_fixture_keys(self) -> None:
        self.client.record("mina", "policy.update", "allowed")
        fixture = self.fixtures["query"]
        self.assertTrue(fixture["response_is_list"])
        events = self.client.query(actor="mina")
        self.assertIsInstance(events, list)
        self.assertTrue(events)
        for event in events:
            self.assertEqual(list(event.keys()), fixture["response_keys"])

    def test_repeated_integrity_calls_return_byte_identical_json_when_state_is_unchanged(self) -> None:
        first = self._raw("GET", "/v1/integrity", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer s3cret"})
        second = self._raw("GET", "/v1/integrity", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer s3cret"})
        self.assertEqual(first, second)

    def test_repeated_query_calls_return_byte_identical_json_when_state_is_unchanged(self) -> None:
        self.client.record("mina", "policy.update", "allowed")
        first = self._raw("GET", "/v1/entries?actor=mina", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer s3cret"})
        second = self._raw("GET", "/v1/entries?actor=mina", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer s3cret"})
        self.assertEqual(first, second)

    def test_bearer_token_as_a_query_parameter_is_not_honored(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as ctx:
            self._raw("GET", "/v1/integrity?access_token=s3cret")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, 401)

    def test_bearer_token_without_the_required_prefix_is_refused(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as ctx:
            self._raw("GET", "/v1/integrity", headers={"Authorization": "s3cret"})
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, 401)

    def test_bearer_token_in_the_request_body_is_not_honored(self) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(
            {"actor": "mina", "action": "x", "outcome": "y", "authorization": "Bearer s3cret"}
        ).encode("utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as ctx:
            self._raw("POST", "/v1/entries", body=body)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, 401)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

1	# Compliance Audit Log starter
2	
3	A small, disposable starter for a local compliance audit-log service. The run
4	prompts grow it into a working service while preserving a stable CLI:
5	
6	```text
7	python -m auditlog.cli record ACTOR ACTION OUTCOME --log-store STORE.db
8	python -m auditlog.cli query --actor ACTOR --log-store STORE.db
9	python -m auditlog.cli repair --log-store STORE.db
10	```
11	
12	The trail is append-only. An entry, once recorded, is never removed, rewritten,
13	or reordered: corrections are made by recording a further entry, not by editing
14	history. Each entry carries a gapless `sequence` and an `event_id` derived
15	deterministically from the entry's own recorded content, so the same content
16	always yields the same id and any later edit is detectable by recomputing it.
17	
18	Two log-store formats exist. The current format records each entry with an
19	explicit content-derived `event_id`. The older archive format used its own
20	`origin_ref` per entry and stored an export-observed `at` value rather than the
21	canonical recording time. It could renumber ids and restamp an event between
22	exports, so overlapping archive batches sometimes contain the same underlying
23	event twice with slightly different `at` values. Reading that format therefore
24	requires deciding when two archived entries are the same event and choosing one
25	representative timestamp deterministically.
26	
27	`metadata` is caller-supplied descriptive context. It is never an input to an
28	entry's identity, and never an input to whether an entry is retained.
29	
30	HTTP routing keeps request-path matching in `auditlog.paths` so
31	authentication and dispatch share one helper. V2 paths are aliases of
32	canonical V1 routes; resolving one through `auditlog.httpd` never yields a
33	weaker bearer requirement than its V1 route has. Client version selection
34	picks which path is called, never whether the call needs a bearer credential:
35	an alias with no declared requirement inherits the V1 route's (defaulting to
36	required if the V1 route is unknown), and an alias with an explicit
37	requirement is still floored by the V1 route, so a stale or mis-declared
38	catalog entry cannot open an unauthenticated path onto data V1 protects.
39	
40	`record`, `query`, and `repair` are written only against the storage-independent
41	`LogStore` contract in `auditlog.service` (`read_only`, `load()`, `save()`), so a
42	new log-store format is added by writing one class that satisfies the
43	contract, not by teaching those functions a new branch. `SqliteLogStore` is
44	that proof: a brand-new `--log-store STORE.db` path becomes a durable SQLite
45	file, where every write commits as its own transaction, so a record made by
46	one process is durably visible to a query made by a separate process. The
47	JSON current and archive formats remain readable (and, for the archive,
48	migratable via `repair`) through the same `open_store` detection, based on
49	each file's own content, never its name.
50	
51	`auditlog.httpd` also runs the one thing actually served over HTTP:
52	bearer-protected V1 routes (`POST /v1/entries`, `GET /v1/entries`, `GET
53	/v1/integrity`) backed by the same `LogStore` contract. `resolve_v1_route` is
54	the single lookup both the auth check and the dispatch use, so there is one
55	route decision, not two. The V2 alias catalog in `auditlog.policy` and its
56	resolution in `auditlog.httpd` are tested but not installed into that
57	server; nothing in the live route table references them. `auditlog.sdk_client`
58	is a small generated V1 client, one method per route, that always sends the
59	bearer credential those routes require.
60	
61	`fixtures/sdk-request-response-fixtures.json` pins the exact request shape
62	(method, path, bearer header placement, body/query keys) and response shape
63	(exact key list, in order) for `record`, `query`, and `integrity`.
64	`tests/test_sdk_fixtures.py` checks the generated client against it two ways:
65	offline, by capturing the `Request` `AuditV1Client` builds without any network
66	call, and live, by running a real V1 server and checking response shape,
67	byte-for-byte JSON stability across repeated calls on unchanged state, and
68	that only the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header authenticates — a token
69	in the query string, the request body, or a header missing the `Bearer`
70	prefix is refused.
71	
72	`auditlog.migration_diagnostics` compares the V1 calls the generated SDK
73	client actually issues against the planned V2 catalog (`auditlog.policy`)
74	entirely offline: `diagnose_migration` is pure data over data (no I/O), so
75	this comparison never sends V2 traffic — there is nothing to send it to, since
76	`create_server` never installs a V2 route. `capture_v1_calls` is the one
77	function that performs I/O, and it only drives the generated V1 client
78	against a live server to record what it actually sends; the recorded shape is
79	also pinned in `fixtures/v1-generated-calls.jsonl`. Runtime routing is
80	unchanged by any of this: the diagnostics module only reads
81	`auditlog.httpd.V1_ROUTES` and `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`, never installs
82	anything.
83
