# Compliance Audit Log starter

A small, disposable starter for a local compliance audit-log service. The run
prompts grow it into a working service while preserving a stable CLI:

```text
python -m auditlog.cli record ACTOR ACTION OUTCOME --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli query --actor ACTOR --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli repair --log-store STORE.db
```

The trail is append-only. An entry, once recorded, is never removed, rewritten,
or reordered: corrections are made by recording a further entry, not by editing
history. Each entry carries a gapless `sequence` and an `event_id` derived
deterministically from the entry's own recorded content, so the same content
always yields the same id and any later edit is detectable by recomputing it.

Two log-store formats exist. The current format records each entry with an
explicit content-derived `event_id`. The older archive format used its own
`origin_ref` per entry and stored an export-observed `at` value rather than the
canonical recording time. It could renumber ids and restamp an event between
exports, so overlapping archive batches sometimes contain the same underlying
event twice with slightly different `at` values. Reading that format therefore
requires deciding when two archived entries are the same event and choosing one
representative timestamp deterministically.

`metadata` is caller-supplied descriptive context. It is never an input to an
entry's identity, and never an input to whether an entry is retained.

HTTP routing keeps request-path matching in `auditlog.paths` so
authentication and dispatch share one helper. V2 paths are aliases of
canonical V1 routes; resolving one through `auditlog.httpd` never yields a
weaker bearer requirement than its V1 route has. Client version selection
picks which path is called, never whether the call needs a bearer credential:
an alias with no declared requirement inherits the V1 route's (defaulting to
required if the V1 route is unknown), and an alias with an explicit
requirement is still floored by the V1 route, so a stale or mis-declared
catalog entry cannot open an unauthenticated path onto data V1 protects.

`record`, `query`, and `repair` are written only against the storage-independent
`LogStore` contract in `auditlog.service` (`read_only`, `load()`, `save()`), so a
new log-store format is added by writing one class that satisfies the
contract, not by teaching those functions a new branch. `SqliteLogStore` is
that proof: a brand-new `--log-store STORE.db` path becomes a durable SQLite
file, where every write commits as its own transaction, so a record made by
one process is durably visible to a query made by a separate process. The
JSON current and archive formats remain readable (and, for the archive,
migratable via `repair`) through the same `open_store` detection, based on
each file's own content, never its name.

`auditlog.httpd` also runs the one thing actually served over HTTP:
bearer-protected V1 routes (`POST /v1/entries`, `GET /v1/entries`, `GET
/v1/integrity`) backed by the same `LogStore` contract. `resolve_v1_route` is
the single lookup both the auth check and the dispatch use, so there is one
route decision, not two. The V2 alias catalog in `auditlog.policy` and its
resolution in `auditlog.httpd` are tested but not installed into that
server; nothing in the live route table references them. `auditlog.sdk_client`
is a small generated V1 client, one method per route, that always sends the
bearer credential those routes require.

`fixtures/sdk-request-response-fixtures.json` pins the exact request shape
(method, path, bearer header placement, body/query keys) and response shape
(exact key list, in order) for `record`, `query`, and `integrity`.
`tests/test_sdk_fixtures.py` checks the generated client against it two ways:
offline, by capturing the `Request` `AuditV1Client` builds without any network
call, and live, by running a real V1 server and checking response shape,
byte-for-byte JSON stability across repeated calls on unchanged state, and
that only the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header authenticates — a token
in the query string, the request body, or a header missing the `Bearer`
prefix is refused.

`auditlog.migration_diagnostics` compares the V1 calls the generated SDK
client actually issues against the planned V2 catalog (`auditlog.policy`)
entirely offline: `diagnose_migration` is pure data over data (no I/O), so
this comparison never sends V2 traffic — there is nothing to send it to, since
`create_server` never installs a V2 route. `capture_v1_calls` is the one
function that performs I/O, and it only drives the generated V1 client
against a live server to record what it actually sends; the recorded shape is
also pinned in `fixtures/v1-generated-calls.jsonl`. Runtime routing is
unchanged by any of this: the diagnostics module only reads
`auditlog.httpd.V1_ROUTES` and `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`, never installs
anything.

`auditlog.migration_reference` renders `docs/sdk-migration-reference.md`
from the compatibility catalog (`auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog`):
one Markdown row per stored catalog row, in the catalog's own order,
preserving each row's method, path, permission, and bearer requirement
exactly (an unset requirement is rendered as unset, never coerced to a
guessed boolean). A second row addressing a (method, path) pair already
seen is rejected rather than silently rendered. Rendering is pure and
offline — it never sends a request or touches what `auditlog.httpd`
serves — and rendering the same catalog twice always produces the same
text; `tests/test_migration_reference.py` checks the committed doc still
matches what the catalog renders today.

`auditlog.migration_checkpoint.CheckpointStore` gives a migration that
drives many generated-client calls a restart-safe record of progress: for
each call's own opaque `call_id` it persists only that id and a `pending`
or `completed` status, in a SQLite file where every write commits as its
own transaction — the same durability `SqliteLogStore` relies on, so a
completion one process marks is immediately visible to a separate process
opened against the same file. It never persists a call's payload, its
response, or the bearer credential used to make it.
`auditlog.migration_replay.replay` drives a list of `ReplayCall`s against
one of these stores: a call already marked complete is never invoked
again, and two calls in one batch can never share a `call_id` that
addresses different calls (`ReplayConflictError`). A call is marked
pending before it is invoked and complete only after, so a crash mid-call
leaves it pending — safe to retry, never falsely complete — for the next
replay, in a separate process if need be, to pick up. Because a V1
record's identity includes the timestamp the server stamps at receipt
(never the client's), a retried `record` call cannot be recognized as
"the same call" by content alone the way an unretried one can; a
`ReplayCall` may supply `already_applied` — a check the caller defines,
such as querying for the record — so a call that already succeeded just
before its checkpoint write was interrupted is marked complete without
being issued again rather than duplicated. None of this ever rewrites or
removes an existing audit record; `tests/test_migration_checkpoint.py`
and `tests/test_migration_replay.py` cover crash recovery, duplicate
replies, conflicting call ids, and continuation from a genuinely separate
OS process.

The project must remain local-only and use the Python standard library. Tests use
`unittest`, so the environment needs no dependency installation.

"""Contract tests for the storage-independent audit-log service.

``record_event`` and ``query_events`` are exercised only through the
``LogStore`` protocol, against both the current and archive formats, so
these tests double as proof that neither function has grown a
format-specific branch.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from auditlog.service import (
    ArchiveLogStore,
    CurrentLogStore,
    IntegrityError,
    LogStore,
    LogStoreError,
    RepairReport,
    SequenceError,
    open_store,
    query_events,
    record_event,
)

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures"


class ContractTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        self.tmp_path = Path(self._tmp.name)

    def _copy_fixture(self, name: str) -> Path:
        dest = self.tmp_path / name
        shutil.copy(FIXTURES / name, dest)
        return dest


class ProtocolComplianceTests(ContractTestCase):
    def test_current_store_satisfies_the_log_store_protocol(self) -> None:
        store = CurrentLogStore(self.tmp_path / "store.json")
        self.assertIsInstance(store, LogStore)
        self.assertFalse(store.read_only)

    def test_archive_store_satisfies_the_log_store_protocol_and_is_read_only(self) -> None:
        store = ArchiveLogStore(self._copy_fixture("legacy-events.json"))
        self.assertIsInstance(store, LogStore)
        self.assertTrue(store.read_only)

    def test_open_store_detects_format_from_store_version(self) -> None:
        current = open_store(self._copy_fixture("current-events.json"))
        legacy = open_store(self._copy_fixture("legacy-events.json"))
        self.assertIsInstance(current, CurrentLogStore)
        self.assertIsInstance(legacy, ArchiveLogStore)

    def test_open_store_rejects_unknown_store_version(self) -> None:
        path = self.tmp_path / "bogus.json"
        path.write_text(json.dumps({"store_version": 99, "entries": []}), encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(LogStoreError):
            open_store(path)


class RecordEventContractTests(ContractTestCase):
    """These run against every writable store format via subTest."""

    def _empty_current_store(self) -> CurrentLogStore:
        return CurrentLogStore(self.tmp_path / "store.json")

    def test_record_event_assigns_gapless_sequence(self) -> None:
        store = self._empty_current_store()
        first = record_event(
            store, actor="a", action="act", outcome="allowed", recorded_at="T1", metadata={}
        )
        second = record_event(
            store, actor="b", action="act", outcome="allowed", recorded_at="T2", metadata={}
        )
        self.assertEqual(first.sequence, 1)
        self.assertEqual(second.sequence, 2)

    def test_recording_identical_content_twice_collapses_to_one_event(self) -> None:
        store = self._empty_current_store()
        first = record_event(
            store, actor="a", action="act", outcome="allowed", recorded_at="T1", metadata={}
        )
        second = record_event(
            store, actor="a", action="act", outcome="allowed", recorded_at="T1", metadata={}
        )
        self.assertEqual(first.event_id, second.event_id)
        self.assertEqual(len(store.load()), 1)

    def test_recording_with_different_metadata_does_not_create_a_second_event(self) -> None:
        store = self._empty_current_store()
        record_event(
            store,
            actor="a",
            action="act",
            outcome="allowed",
            recorded_at="T1",
            metadata={"note": "first"},
        )
        record_event(
            store,
            actor="a",
            action="act",
            outcome="allowed",
            recorded_at="T1",
            metadata={"note": "second"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(store.load()), 1)

    def test_cannot_record_into_a_read_only_archive_store(self) -> None:
        store = ArchiveLogStore(self._copy_fixture("legacy-events.json"))
        with self.assertRaises(LogStoreError):
            record_event(
                store, actor="a", action="act", outcome="allowed", recorded_at="T1", metadata={}
            )

    def test_query_filters_by_actor_and_action(self) -> None:

        record_event(store, actor="mina", action="policy.update", outcome="allowed", recorded_at="T1", metadata={})
        record_event(store, actor="sven", action="key.revoke", outcome="allowed", recorded_at="T2", metadata={})

        self.assertEqual(len(query_events(store, actor="mina")), 2)

        self.assertEqual(len(query_events(store, actor="mina", action="key.revoke")), 1)

    def test_query_against_the_archive_format_dedups_and_sorts(self) -> None:
        store = ArchiveLogStore(self._copy_fixture("legacy-events.json"))
        events = query_events(store)

            keys,
            {
                ("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed"),
                ("operator:sven", "key.revoke", "allowed"),

        store = ArchiveLogStore(self._copy_fixture("legacy-events.json"))
        events = query_events(store, actor="operator:mina")

        self.assertEqual(events[0].recorded_at, "2024-03-02T10:15:00Z")
        self.assertEqual(sorted(events[0].metadata["origin_refs"]), ["arch-1001", "arch-2001"])


class IntegrityAndSequenceTests(ContractTestCase):
    def test_tampered_content_is_detected_on_load(self) -> None:
        path = self._copy_fixture("current-events.json")
        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        raw["entries"][0]["outcome"] = "denied"
        path.write_text(json.dumps(raw), encoding="utf-8")

        with self.assertRaises(IntegrityError):
            CurrentLogStore(path).load()

    def test_non_gapless_sequence_is_detected_on_load(self) -> None:
        path = self._copy_fixture("current-events.json")
        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        raw["entries"][1]["sequence"] = 5
        path.write_text(json.dumps(raw), encoding="utf-8")

"""Characterization tests for the deliberately small starter."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from auditlog.cli import build_parser
from auditlog.models import AuditEvent, content_digest


class StarterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_identity_is_the_recorded_content(self) -> None:
        first = content_digest("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T1")
        same = content_digest("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T1")
        later = content_digest("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T2")
        self.assertEqual(first, same)
        self.assertNotEqual(first, later)

    def test_recomputed_id_detects_an_edited_entry(self) -> None:
        actor, action, outcome, at = "operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T1"
        entry = AuditEvent(content_digest(actor, action, outcome, at), 1, actor, action, outcome, at)
        self.assertEqual(entry.event_id, entry.recomputed_id())
        edited = AuditEvent(entry.event_id, 1, actor, action, "denied", at)
        self.assertNotEqual(edited.event_id, edited.recomputed_id())

    def test_public_commands_exist(self) -> None:
        parser = build_parser()
        choices = parser._subparsers._group_actions[0].choices
        self.assertEqual(set(choices), {"record", "query", "repair"})

    def test_archive_duplicate_has_export_time_drift(self) -> None:
        fixture_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures" / "legacy-events.json"
        fixture = json.loads(fixture_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        first, second = fixture["entries"][:2]

        stable_fields = ("actor", "action", "outcome")
        for field in stable_fields:
            self.assertEqual(first[field], second[field])
        self.assertNotEqual(first["at"], second["at"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

from __future__ import annotations

import http.server
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs

from .paths import auth_path
from .service import (
    IntegrityError,
    LogStore,
    LogStoreError,
    SequenceError,
    open_store,
    query_events,
    record_event,
)
from .timeutil import now_utc


def resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...], canonical_bearer: dict[tuple[str, str], bool]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool], ...]:
    """Resolve inherited aliases through their canonical V1 route keys.

    The result is the canonical V1 route's requirement OR'd with whatever the
    alias entry declares, so version selection can add a bearer requirement
    but never remove one.
    """

    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]] = []
    for method, path, permission, requires_auth in catalog:
        canonical_path = path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1)
        canonical_requires_auth = canonical_bearer.get((method, canonical_path), True)
        effective_requires_auth = canonical_requires_auth or bool(requires_auth)
        resolved.append((method, path, permission, effective_requires_auth))
    return tuple(resolved)


# --- Bearer-protected V1 routes: the only routes actually served -----------

V1_ROUTES: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, bool]] = {
    ("POST", "/v1/entries"): ("record", True),
    ("GET", "/v1/entries"): ("query", True),
    ("GET", "/v1/integrity"): ("integrity", True),
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RouteDecision:
    permission: str
    requires_auth: bool


def resolve_v1_route(method: str, raw_path: str) -> RouteDecision | None:
    """The one lookup the auth check and the dispatch both use.

    ``auth_path`` is the same helper ``dispatch_path`` wraps (see
    ``auditlog.paths``), so there is exactly one canonical spelling of the
    request path in play. This function turns that one spelling into one
    route decision, and the handler below reuses it for both the auth check
    and the dispatch instead of resolving the route twice.
    """

    path_only, _, _ = raw_path.partition("?")
    path = auth_path(path_only)
    entry = V1_ROUTES.get((method, path))
    if entry is None:
        return None
    permission, requires_auth = entry
    return RouteDecision(permission=permission, requires_auth=requires_auth)


class AuditHTTPServer(http.server.HTTPServer):
    """An ``HTTPServer`` carrying the one log store and bearer token it serves."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        server_address: tuple[str, int],
        handler_class: type[http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler],
        *,
        store: LogStore,
        bearer_token: str,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(server_address, handler_class)
        self.store = store
        self.bearer_token = bearer_token


class V1RequestHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Serves the bearer-protected V1 routes; refuses anything else."""

    server: AuditHTTPServer

    def _authorized(self) -> bool:
        return self.headers.get("Authorization") == f"Bearer {self.server.bearer_token}"

    def _write_json(self, status: int, payload: object) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _handle(self, method: str) -> None:
        decision = resolve_v1_route(method, self.path)
        if decision is None:
            self._write_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
            return
        if decision.requires_auth and not self._authorized():
            self._write_json(401, {"error": "bearer credential required"})
            return
        try:
            self._dispatch(decision.permission)
        except (LogStoreError, IntegrityError, SequenceError) as exc:
            self._write_json(409, {"error": str(exc)})

    def _dispatch(self, permission: str) -> None:
        _, _, query_string = self.path.partition("?")
        if permission == "record":
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
            event = record_event(
                self.server.store,
                actor=body["actor"],
                action=body["action"],
                outcome=body["outcome"],
                recorded_at=now_utc(),
                metadata=body.get("metadata", {}),
            )
            self._write_json(200, event.to_record())
        elif permission == "query":
            params = parse_qs(query_string)
            events = query_events(
                self.server.store,
                actor=(params.get("actor") or [None])[0],
                action=(params.get("action") or [None])[0],
            )
            self._write_json(200, [event.to_record() for event in events])
        else:  # "integrity"
            events = self.server.store.load()
            self._write_json(200, {"ok": True, "event_count": len(events)})

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        self._handle("POST")

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        self._handle("GET")

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:  # quiet during tests
        pass


def create_server(
    log_store_path: Path, bearer_token: str, *, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 0
) -> AuditHTTPServer:
    """Build the V1-only server. The V2 alias catalog is not installed here."""

    store = open_store(log_store_path)
    return AuditHTTPServer((host, port), V1RequestHandler, store=store, bearer_token=bearer_token)

"""The host transport: bearer-protected V1 routes, plus the installed V2 aliases.

``resolve_v2_alias_catalog`` is a stable, offline resolution seam for
compatibility work: given a V2 alias catalog and the canonical V1 routes'
bearer requirements, it computes what each alias's effective requirement
would be. ``create_server`` calls it at server startup, against the turn-3
catalog (``auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog``) and the live
``V1_ROUTES`` bearer table, and installs the resolved aliases on the server
it builds — so every server this module creates now serves both the V1
routes and their resolved V2 aliases side by side.

A client selects a V2 alias by which path it calls, never by which bearer
requirement applies to that call: the resolved requirement can only ever be
at least as strict as the alias's canonical V1 route, never weaker. An alias
left unset (``requires_auth is None``) inherits the canonical route's
requirement, defaulting to required when the canonical route itself is
unknown. An alias that declares its requirement explicitly is still floored
by the canonical route, so a stale or mis-declared catalog entry (or a
client that negotiates an older SDK version) cannot open an unauthenticated
path onto data the V1 route protects. A request that matches neither a V1
route nor an installed V2 alias is still unknown, exactly as before.

from __future__ import annotations

import http.server
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs

from .paths import auth_path
from .policy import build_v2_alias_catalog
from .service import (

    SequenceError,

def resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...], canonical_bearer: dict[tuple[str, str], bool]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool], ...]:
    """Resolve inherited aliases through their canonical V1 route keys.

    The result is the canonical V1 route's requirement OR'd with whatever the
    alias entry declares, so version selection can add a bearer requirement
    but never remove one.
    """

    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]] = []
    for method, path, permission, requires_auth in catalog:
        canonical_path = path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1)
        canonical_requires_auth = canonical_bearer.get((method, canonical_path), True)
        effective_requires_auth = canonical_requires_auth or bool(requires_auth)
        resolved.append((method, path, permission, effective_requires_auth))
    return tuple(resolved)

    ("POST", "/v1/entries"): ("record", True),

    permission: str
    requires_auth: bool


def resolve_v1_route(method: str, raw_path: str) -> RouteDecision | None:

    request path in play. This function turns that one spelling into one
    route decision, and the handler below reuses it for both the auth check
    and the dispatch instead of resolving the route twice.
    """

    path_only, _, _ = raw_path.partition("?")
    path = auth_path(path_only)
    entry = V1_ROUTES.get((method, path))
    if entry is None:
        return None
    permission, requires_auth = entry
    return RouteDecision(permission=permission, requires_auth=requires_auth)

    """The live V1 bearer table, keyed the way ``resolve_v2_alias_catalog`` wants it."""

    return {

    }


def resolve_v2_routes(
    catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...],

    return {
        (method, path): (permission, requires_auth)
        for method, path, permission, requires_auth in resolved

    entry = v2_routes.get((method, path))
    if entry is None:

    permission, requires_auth = entry

"""Command-line shell for the audit log service.

Each command is a thin adapter onto ``auditlog.service``: the CLI parses
arguments and formats output, and the service functions carry all of the
storage-independent behavior (identity, sequencing, integrity, repair).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from .service import LogStoreError, open_store, query_events, record_event
from .timeutil import now_utc


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Return the stable top-level parser the acceptance path imports.

    The ``record``/``query``/``repair`` commands and their required
    ``--log-store`` option are the documented contract; keep them.
    """

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="auditlog")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    record = subparsers.add_parser("record", help="append an entry to the trail")
    record.add_argument("actor")
    record.add_argument("action")
    record.add_argument("outcome")
    record.add_argument(
        "--metadata",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="KEY=VALUE",
        help="descriptive context to store with the entry; repeatable",
    )
    record.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    query = subparsers.add_parser("query", help="read entries from the trail")
    query.add_argument("--actor")
    query.add_argument("--action")
    query.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    repair = subparsers.add_parser("repair", help="rebuild derived indexes")
    repair.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)
    return parser


def _parse_metadata(pairs: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Turn repeated ``KEY=VALUE`` options into the metadata dict callers see."""

    metadata: dict[str, str] = {}
    for pair in pairs:
        key, sep, value = pair.partition("=")
        if not sep:
            raise ValueError(f"--metadata expects KEY=VALUE, got {pair!r}")
        metadata[key] = value
    return metadata


def _run_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    event = record_event(
        store,
        actor=args.actor,
        action=args.action,
        outcome=args.outcome,
        recorded_at=now_utc(),
        metadata=_parse_metadata(args.metadata),
    )
    print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_query(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    for event in query_events(store, actor=args.actor, action=args.action):
        print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_repair(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    report = store.repair()
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "event_count": report.event_count,
                "resequenced": report.resequenced,
                "migrated_from_archive": report.migrated_from_archive,
            }
        )
    )
    return 0


_HANDLERS = {"record": _run_record, "query": _run_query, "repair": _run_repair}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse the command line and dispatch to the matching command handler."""

    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return _HANDLERS[args.command](args)
    except (LogStoreError, ValueError) as exc:
        parser.error(str(exc))
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Return the stable top-level parser the acceptance path imports.

    The ``record``/``query``/``repair`` commands and their required
    ``--log-store`` option are the documented contract; keep them. ``serve``
    exposes the same loopback server ``auditlog.httpd.create_server`` builds
    (bearer-protected V1 routes plus the installed V2 aliases) and reads
    from and writes to that same ``--log-store`` path and format, so a
    ``query`` run afterward against the same path sees what ``serve``
    recorded.
    """

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="auditlog")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    record = subparsers.add_parser("record", help="append an entry to the trail")
    record.add_argument("actor")
    record.add_argument("action")
    record.add_argument("outcome")
    record.add_argument(
        "--metadata",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="KEY=VALUE",
        help="descriptive context to store with the entry; repeatable",
    )
    record.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    query = subparsers.add_parser("query", help="read entries from the trail")
    query.add_argument("--actor")
    query.add_argument("--action")
    query.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    repair = subparsers.add_parser("repair", help="rebuild derived indexes")
    repair.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    serve = subparsers.add_parser(
        "serve", help="run the loopback HTTP server (V1 routes plus installed V2 aliases)"
    )
    serve.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--bearer-token", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=0)
    return parser


def _parse_metadata(pairs: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Turn repeated ``KEY=VALUE`` options into the metadata dict callers see."""

    metadata: dict[str, str] = {}
    for pair in pairs:
        key, sep, value = pair.partition("=")
        if not sep:
            raise ValueError(f"--metadata expects KEY=VALUE, got {pair!r}")
        metadata[key] = value
    return metadata


def _run_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    event = record_event(
        store,
        actor=args.actor,
        action=args.action,
        outcome=args.outcome,
        recorded_at=now_utc(),
        metadata=_parse_metadata(args.metadata),
    )
    print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_query(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    for event in query_events(store, actor=args.actor, action=args.action):
        print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_repair(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    report = store.repair()
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "event_count": report.event_count,
                "resequenced": report.resequenced,
                "migrated_from_archive": report.migrated_from_archive,
            }
        )
    )
    return 0


_HANDLERS = {"record": _run_record, "query": _run_query, "repair": _run_repair}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse the command line and dispatch to the matching command handler."""

    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return _HANDLERS[args.command](args)
    except (LogStoreError, ValueError) as exc:
        parser.error(str(exc))
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

``resolve_v2_alias_catalog`` is a stable, offline resolution seam for
compatibility work: given a V2 alias catalog and the canonical V1 routes'
bearer requirements, it computes what each alias's effective requirement
would be. ``create_server`` calls it at server startup, against the turn-3
catalog (``auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog``) and the live
``V1_ROUTES`` bearer table, and installs the resolved aliases on the server
it builds — so every server this module creates now serves both the V1
routes and their resolved V2 aliases side by side.

A client selects a V2 alias by which path it calls, never by which bearer
requirement applies to that call: the resolved requirement can only ever be
at least as strict as the alias's canonical V1 route, never weaker. An alias
left unset (``requires_auth is None``) inherits the canonical route's
requirement, defaulting to required when the canonical route itself is
unknown. An alias that declares its requirement explicitly is still floored
by the canonical route, so a stale or mis-declared catalog entry (or a
client that negotiates an older SDK version) cannot open an unauthenticated
path onto data the V1 route protects. A request that matches neither a V1
route nor an installed V2 alias is still unknown, exactly as before.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import http.server
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs

from .paths import auth_path
from .policy import build_v2_alias_catalog
from .service import (
    IntegrityError,
    LogStore,
    LogStoreError,
    SequenceError,
    open_store,
    query_events,
    record_event,
)
from .timeutil import now_utc


def resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...], canonical_bearer: dict[tuple[str, str], bool]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool], ...]:
    """Resolve inherited aliases through their canonical V1 route keys.

    The result is the canonical V1 route's requirement OR'd with whatever the
    alias entry declares, so version selection can add a bearer requirement
    but never remove one.
    """

    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]] = []
    for method, path, permission, requires_auth in catalog:
        canonical_path = path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1)
        canonical_requires_auth = canonical_bearer.get((method, canonical_path), True)
        effective_requires_auth = canonical_requires_auth or bool(requires_auth)
        resolved.append((method, path, permission, effective_requires_auth))
    return tuple(resolved)


# --- Bearer-protected V1 routes: the only routes actually served -----------

V1_ROUTES: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, bool]] = {
    ("POST", "/v1/entries"): ("record", True),
    ("GET", "/v1/entries"): ("query", True),
    ("GET", "/v1/integrity"): ("integrity", True),
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RouteDecision:
    permission: str
    requires_auth: bool


def resolve_v1_route(method: str, raw_path: str) -> RouteDecision | None:
    """The one lookup the auth check and the dispatch both use.

    ``auth_path`` is the same helper ``dispatch_path`` wraps (see
    ``auditlog.paths``), so there is exactly one canonical spelling of the
    request path in play. This function turns that one spelling into one
    route decision, and the handler below reuses it for both the auth check
    and the dispatch instead of resolving the route twice.
    """

    path_only, _, _ = raw_path.partition("?")
    path = auth_path(path_only)
    entry = V1_ROUTES.get((method, path))
    if entry is None:
        return None
    permission, requires_auth = entry
    return RouteDecision(permission=permission, requires_auth=requires_auth)


def _v1_canonical_bearer() -> dict[tuple[str, str], bool]:
    """The live V1 bearer table, keyed the way ``resolve_v2_alias_catalog`` wants it."""

    return {
        (method, path): requires_auth
        for (method, path), (_permission, requires_auth) in V1_ROUTES.items()
    }


def resolve_v2_routes(
    catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...],
) -> dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, bool]]:
    """Resolve a V2 alias catalog into an installable route table.

    Floors every alias through the live V1 bearer table (``V1_ROUTES``), the
    same non-weakening rule ``resolve_v2_alias_catalog`` always applies, so
    the result is safe to install alongside ``V1_ROUTES`` on a real server.
    """

    resolved = resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog, _v1_canonical_bearer())
    return {
        (method, path): (permission, requires_auth)
        for method, path, permission, requires_auth in resolved
    }


def resolve_v2_route(
    method: str, raw_path: str, v2_routes: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, bool]]
) -> RouteDecision | None:
    """The V2 counterpart to ``resolve_v1_route``, looked up in installed aliases."""

    path_only, _, _ = raw_path.partition("?")
    path = auth_path(path_only)
    entry = v2_routes.get((method, path))
    if entry is None:
        return None
    permission, requires_auth = entry
    return RouteDecision(permission=permission, requires_auth=requires_auth)


class AuditHTTPServer(http.server.HTTPServer):
    """An ``HTTPServer`` carrying the one log store, bearer token, and installed
    V2 alias table it serves."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        server_address: tuple[str, int],
        handler_class: type[http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler],
        *,
        store: LogStore,
        bearer_token: str,
        v2_routes: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, bool]],
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(server_address, handler_class)
        self.store = store
        self.bearer_token = bearer_token
        self.v2_routes = v2_routes


class V1RequestHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Serves the bearer-protected V1 routes and the installed V2 aliases;
    refuses anything else."""

    server: AuditHTTPServer

    def _authorized(self) -> bool:
        return self.headers.get("Authorization") == f"Bearer {self.server.bearer_token}"

    def _write_json(self, status: int, payload: object) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _handle(self, method: str) -> None:
        decision = resolve_v1_route(method, self.path)
        if decision is None:
            decision = resolve_v2_route(method, self.path, self.server.v2_routes)
        if decision is None:
            self._write_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
            return
        if decision.requires_auth and not self._authorized():
            self._write_json(401, {"error": "bearer credential required"})
            return
        try:
            self._dispatch(decision.permission)
        except (LogStoreError, IntegrityError, SequenceError) as exc:
            self._write_json(409, {"error": str(exc)})

    def _dispatch(self, permission: str) -> None:
        _, _, query_string = self.path.partition("?")
        if permission == "record":
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
            event = record_event(
                self.server.store,
                actor=body["actor"],
                action=body["action"],
                outcome=body["outcome"],
                recorded_at=now_utc(),
                metadata=body.get("metadata", {}),
            )
            self._write_json(200, event.to_record())
        elif permission == "query":
            params = parse_qs(query_string)
            events = query_events(
                self.server.store,
                actor=(params.get("actor") or [None])[0],
                action=(params.get("action") or [None])[0],
            )
            self._write_json(200, [event.to_record() for event in events])
        else:  # "integrity"
            events = self.server.store.load()
            self._write_json(200, {"ok": True, "event_count": len(events)})

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        self._handle("POST")

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        self._handle("GET")

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:  # quiet during tests
        pass


def create_server(
    log_store_path: Path, bearer_token: str, *, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 0
) -> AuditHTTPServer:
    """Build the server: bearer-protected V1 routes plus the resolved V2 aliases.

    The turn-3 catalog (``auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog``) is
    resolved through the live V1 bearer table and installed on the server at
    startup, so a V2 alias is reachable and exactly as strictly
    bearer-protected as the V1 route it aliases.
    """

    store = open_store(log_store_path)
    v2_routes = resolve_v2_routes(build_v2_alias_catalog())
    return AuditHTTPServer(
        (host, port), V1RequestHandler, store=store, bearer_token=bearer_token, v2_routes=v2_routes
    )

3	Adding a route to that table is the only edit a real generator would need
4	to add a client method here. ``api_version`` selects which resolved path
5	each call addresses — ``"v1"`` (the default) or ``"v2"`` for the aliases
6	``auditlog.httpd.create_server`` installs — without changing how the bearer
7	credential is sent: every call still sends the same
8	``Authorization: Bearer <token>`` header regardless of version, and the
9	client has no way to ask for a route without one.
10	"""

15	import urllib.request
16	from urllib.parse import urlencode

19	class AuditV1Client:
20	    """Generated client for the bearer-protected audit-log routes."""
21	
22	    def __init__(self, base_url: str, bearer_token: str, *, api_version: str = "v1") -> None:
23	        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
24	        self._bearer_token = bearer_token
25	        self._api_version = api_version
26	
27	    def _versioned(self, path_suffix: str) -> str:
28	        return f"/{self._api_version}{path_suffix}"
29	
30	    def _request(
31	        self,
32	        method: str,
33	        path: str,
34	        *,
35	        query: dict[str, str] | None = None,
36	        body: dict[str, object] | None = None,
37	    ) -> object:
38	        url = f"{self._base_url}{path}"
39	        if query:
40	            url = f"{url}?{urlencode(query)}"
41	        data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else None
42	        request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
43	        request.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {self._bearer_token}")
44	        if data is not None:
45	            request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
46	        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
47	            return json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))

"""Command-line shell for the audit log service.

Each command is a thin adapter onto ``auditlog.service``: the CLI parses
arguments and formats output, and the service functions carry all of the
storage-independent behavior (identity, sequencing, integrity, repair).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from .httpd import create_server
from .service import LogStoreError, open_store, query_events, record_event
from .timeutil import now_utc


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Return the stable top-level parser the acceptance path imports.

    The ``record``/``query``/``repair`` commands and their required
    ``--log-store`` option are the documented contract; keep them. ``serve``
    exposes the same loopback server ``auditlog.httpd.create_server`` builds
    (bearer-protected V1 routes plus the installed V2 aliases) and reads
    from and writes to that same ``--log-store`` path and format, so a
    ``query`` run afterward against the same path sees what ``serve``
    recorded.
    """

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="auditlog")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    record = subparsers.add_parser("record", help="append an entry to the trail")
    record.add_argument("actor")
    record.add_argument("action")
    record.add_argument("outcome")
    record.add_argument(
        "--metadata",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="KEY=VALUE",
        help="descriptive context to store with the entry; repeatable",
    )
    record.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    query = subparsers.add_parser("query", help="read entries from the trail")
    query.add_argument("--actor")
    query.add_argument("--action")
    query.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    repair = subparsers.add_parser("repair", help="rebuild derived indexes")
    repair.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    serve = subparsers.add_parser(
        "serve", help="run the loopback HTTP server (V1 routes plus installed V2 aliases)"
    )
    serve.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--bearer-token", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=0)
    return parser


def _parse_metadata(pairs: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Turn repeated ``KEY=VALUE`` options into the metadata dict callers see."""

    metadata: dict[str, str] = {}
    for pair in pairs:
        key, sep, value = pair.partition("=")
        if not sep:
            raise ValueError(f"--metadata expects KEY=VALUE, got {pair!r}")
        metadata[key] = value
    return metadata


def _run_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    event = record_event(
        store,
        actor=args.actor,
        action=args.action,
        outcome=args.outcome,
        recorded_at=now_utc(),
        metadata=_parse_metadata(args.metadata),
    )
    print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_query(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    for event in query_events(store, actor=args.actor, action=args.action):
        print(json.dumps(event.to_record()))
    return 0


def _run_repair(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    store = open_store(Path(args.log_store))
    report = store.repair()
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "event_count": report.event_count,
                "resequenced": report.resequenced,
                "migrated_from_archive": report.migrated_from_archive,
            }
        )
    )
    return 0


_HANDLERS = {"record": _run_record, "query": _run_query, "repair": _run_repair}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse the command line and dispatch to the matching command handler."""

    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return _HANDLERS[args.command](args)
    except (LogStoreError, ValueError) as exc:
        parser.error(str(exc))
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Characterization tests for the deliberately small starter."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from auditlog.cli import build_parser
from auditlog.models import AuditEvent, content_digest


class StarterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_identity_is_the_recorded_content(self) -> None:
        first = content_digest("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T1")
        same = content_digest("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T1")
        later = content_digest("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T2")
        self.assertEqual(first, same)
        self.assertNotEqual(first, later)

    def test_recomputed_id_detects_an_edited_entry(self) -> None:
        actor, action, outcome, at = "operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "T1"
        entry = AuditEvent(content_digest(actor, action, outcome, at), 1, actor, action, outcome, at)
        self.assertEqual(entry.event_id, entry.recomputed_id())
        edited = AuditEvent(entry.event_id, 1, actor, action, "denied", at)
        self.assertNotEqual(edited.event_id, edited.recomputed_id())

    def test_public_commands_exist(self) -> None:
        parser = build_parser()
        choices = parser._subparsers._group_actions[0].choices
        self.assertEqual(set(choices), {"record", "query", "repair"})

    def test_archive_duplicate_has_export_time_drift(self) -> None:
        fixture_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures" / "legacy-events.json"
        fixture = json.loads(fixture_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        first, second = fixture["entries"][:2]

        stable_fields = ("actor", "action", "outcome")
        for field in stable_fields:
            self.assertEqual(first[field], second[field])
        self.assertNotEqual(first["at"], second["at"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class V2CatalogTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_catalog_returns_the_three_fixed_v2_rows_with_explicit_true(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            build_v2_alias_catalog(),
            (
                ("POST", "/v2/entries", "record", True),
                ("GET", "/v2/entries", "query", True),
                ("GET", "/v2/integrity", "integrity", True),
            ),

class V1RouteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        store_path = Path(self._tmp.name) / "store.db"

        self.server = create_server(store_path, "s3cret", port=0)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._shutdown)
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"

    def _shutdown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.thread.join()
        self.server.server_close()

    def test_request_without_a_bearer_token_is_refused(self) -> None:
        request = urllib.request.Request(f"{self.base_url}/v1/entries", method="GET")

        self.assertEqual(recorded["sequence"], 1)

        events = client.query(actor="mina")
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0]["event_id"], recorded["event_id"])

"""Migration diagnostics: generated V1 calls vs. the planned V2 catalog.

None of this sends V2 traffic. ``auditlog.httpd.create_server`` never
installs a V2 route, so there is nothing to send V2 traffic to; the
"planned V2 calls" side here is always the offline catalog data
(``auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog``), and ``diagnose_migration``
itself performs no I/O at all (checked directly below). The one function
that does perform I/O, ``capture_v1_calls``, only ever drives the generated
V1 SDK client against a live, V1-only server.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from auditlog.httpd import create_server
from auditlog.migration_diagnostics import (
    GeneratedCall,
    capture_v1_calls,
    diagnose_migration,
)
from auditlog.policy import build_v2_alias_catalog

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures"


def _load_fixture_calls() -> tuple:
    lines = (FIXTURES / "v1-generated-calls.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    raw_calls = [json.loads(line) for line in lines if line.strip()]
    return tuple(
        GeneratedCall(
            method=call["method"],
            path=call["path"],
            used_bearer=call["credential_mode"] == "bearer",
        )
        for call in raw_calls
    )


class OfflineDiagnosticsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_recorded_v1_calls_fixture_matches_the_planned_v2_catalog_with_no_discrepancies(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        discrepancies = diagnose_migration(_load_fixture_calls(), build_v2_alias_catalog())
        self.assertEqual(discrepancies, ())

    def test_diagnose_migration_never_touches_the_network(self) -> None:
        real_urlopen = urllib.request.urlopen

        def _forbidden(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> None:
            raise AssertionError("diagnose_migration must not perform network I/O")

        urllib.request.urlopen = _forbidden
        try:
            diagnose_migration(_load_fixture_calls(), build_v2_alias_catalog())
        finally:
            urllib.request.urlopen = real_urlopen

    def test_a_generated_call_missing_its_bearer_credential_is_flagged(self) -> None:
        calls = (GeneratedCall(method="POST", path="/v1/entries", used_bearer=False),)
        catalog = (("POST", "/v2/entries", "record", True),)
        discrepancies = diagnose_migration(calls, catalog)
        self.assertEqual(len(discrepancies), 1)
        self.assertIn("bearer", discrepancies[0].reason)

    def test_a_generated_call_with_no_planned_v2_alias_is_flagged(self) -> None:
        calls = (GeneratedCall(method="DELETE", path="/v1/entries", used_bearer=True),)
        discrepancies = diagnose_migration(calls, build_v2_alias_catalog())
        matches = [d for d in discrepancies if d.method == "DELETE" and d.v1_path == "/v1/entries"]
        self.assertEqual(len(matches), 1)
        self.assertIn("no planned V2 alias", matches[0].reason)

    def test_a_planned_v2_alias_with_no_generated_v1_call_is_flagged(self) -> None:
        catalog = build_v2_alias_catalog() + (("GET", "/v2/new-thing", "new-thing", True),)
        discrepancies = diagnose_migration(_load_fixture_calls(), catalog)
        reasons = {d.reason for d in discrepancies}
        self.assertIn("planned V2 alias has no observed generated V1 call", reasons)

    def test_an_in_sync_call_produces_no_discrepancy(self) -> None:
        calls = (GeneratedCall(method="POST", path="/v1/entries", used_bearer=True),)
        catalog = (("POST", "/v2/entries", "record", True),)
        self.assertEqual(diagnose_migration(calls, catalog), ())


class LiveCaptureTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Confirm the fixture matches what the real SDK client actually sends today."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        store_path = Path(self._tmp.name) / "store.db"
        self.server = create_server(store_path, "s3cret", port=0)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._shutdown)
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"

    def _shutdown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.thread.join()
        self.server.server_close()

    def test_capturing_the_live_client_yields_only_v1_paths(self) -> None:
        captured = capture_v1_calls(self.base_url, "s3cret")
        self.assertTrue(captured)
        for call in captured:
            self.assertTrue(call.path.startswith("/v1/"))
            self.assertNotIn("/v2/", call.path)

    def test_capturing_the_live_client_matches_the_versioned_fixture(self) -> None:
        captured = capture_v1_calls(self.base_url, "s3cret")
        fixture_calls = _load_fixture_calls()
        self.assertEqual(
            {(c.method, c.path) for c in captured},
            {(c.method, c.path) for c in fixture_calls},
        )
        self.assertTrue(all(c.used_bearer for c in captured))

    def test_diagnosing_the_captured_calls_against_the_planned_catalog_has_no_discrepancies(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        captured = capture_v1_calls(self.base_url, "s3cret")
        discrepancies = diagnose_migration(captured, build_v2_alias_catalog())
        self.assertEqual(discrepancies, ())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Integration test for ``python -m auditlog.cli serve``.

Proves: the ``serve`` subcommand exposes the same server
``auditlog.httpd.create_server`` builds (bearer-protected V1 routes plus the
installed V2 aliases), takes ``--log-store``, ``--bearer-token``, ``--host``,
and ``--port`` exactly as documented, and writes into the same durable store
format and path the ``query`` subcommand reads — a record made over HTTP
while ``serve`` runs is visible to a ``query`` run as a separate process
against the same ``--log-store`` path.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


class ServeSubcommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        self.store_path = Path(self._tmp.name) / "store.db"
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-m",
                "auditlog.cli",
                "serve",
                "--log-store",
                str(self.store_path),
                "--bearer-token",
                "s3cret",
                "--host",
                "127.0.0.1",
                "--port",
                "0",
            ],
            cwd=str(REPO_ROOT),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
        )
        self.addCleanup(self._stop)
        announcement = json.loads(self.process.stdout.readline())
        self.base_url = f"http://{announcement['host']}:{announcement['port']}"

    def _stop(self) -> None:
        self.process.terminate()
        self.process.wait(timeout=5)

    def _status(self, method: str, path: str, *, bearer: str | None) -> int:
        request = urllib.request.Request(f"{self.base_url}{path}", method=method)
        if bearer is not None:
            request.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {bearer}")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
                return response.status
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code

    def test_serve_exposes_v1_and_the_installed_v2_aliases_over_the_documented_flags(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v1/integrity", bearer="s3cret"), 200)
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v2/integrity", bearer="s3cret"), 200)
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v1/integrity", bearer=None), 401)
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v2/integrity", bearer=None), 401)

    def test_serve_and_query_share_one_durable_store_at_the_same_path(self) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(
            {"actor": "mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed"}
        ).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request(f"{self.base_url}/v1/entries", data=body, method="POST")
        request.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer s3cret")
        request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request):
            pass

        result = subprocess.run(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-m",
                "auditlog.cli",
                "query",
                "--actor",
                "mina",
                "--log-store",
                str(self.store_path),
            ],
            cwd=str(REPO_ROOT),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
        records = [json.loads(line) for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
        self.assertEqual(len(records), 1)
        self.assertEqual(records[0]["actor"], "mina")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Integration test for ``python -m auditlog.cli serve``.

Proves: the ``serve`` subcommand exposes the same server
``auditlog.httpd.create_server`` builds (bearer-protected V1 routes plus the
installed V2 aliases), takes ``--log-store``, ``--bearer-token``, ``--host``,
and ``--port`` exactly as documented, and writes into the same durable store
format and path the ``query`` subcommand reads — a record made over HTTP
while ``serve`` runs is visible to a ``query`` run as a separate process
against the same ``--log-store`` path.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


class ServeSubcommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        self.store_path = Path(self._tmp.name) / "store.db"
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-m",
                "auditlog.cli",
                "serve",
                "--log-store",
                str(self.store_path),
                "--bearer-token",
                "s3cret",
                "--host",
                "127.0.0.1",
                "--port",
                "0",
            ],
            cwd=str(REPO_ROOT),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
        )
        self.addCleanup(self._stop)
        announcement = json.loads(self.process.stdout.readline())
        self.base_url = f"http://{announcement['host']}:{announcement['port']}"

    def _stop(self) -> None:
        self.process.terminate()
        self.process.wait(timeout=5)

    def _status(self, method: str, path: str, *, bearer: str | None) -> int:
        request = urllib.request.Request(f"{self.base_url}{path}", method=method)
        if bearer is not None:
            request.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {bearer}")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
                return response.status
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code

    def test_serve_exposes_v1_and_the_installed_v2_aliases_over_the_documented_flags(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v1/integrity", bearer="s3cret"), 200)
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v2/integrity", bearer="s3cret"), 200)
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v1/integrity", bearer=None), 401)
        self.assertEqual(self._status("GET", "/v2/integrity", bearer=None), 401)

    def test_serve_and_query_share_one_durable_store_at_the_same_path(self) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(
            {"actor": "mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed"}
        ).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request(f"{self.base_url}/v1/entries", data=body, method="POST")
        request.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer s3cret")
        request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request):
            pass

        result = subprocess.run(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-m",
                "auditlog.cli",
                "query",
                "--actor",
                "mina",
                "--log-store",
                str(self.store_path),
            ],
            cwd=str(REPO_ROOT),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
        records = [json.loads(line) for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
        self.assertEqual(len(records), 1)
        self.assertEqual(records[0]["actor"], "mina")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Compliance Audit Log starter

A small, disposable starter for a local compliance audit-log service. The run
prompts grow it into a working service while preserving a stable CLI:

```text
python -m auditlog.cli record ACTOR ACTION OUTCOME --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli query --actor ACTOR --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli repair --log-store STORE.db
```

The trail is append-only. An entry, once recorded, is never removed, rewritten,
or reordered: corrections are made by recording a further entry, not by editing
history. Each entry carries a gapless `sequence` and an `event_id` derived
deterministically from the entry's own recorded content, so the same content
always yields the same id and any later edit is detectable by recomputing it.

Two log-store formats exist. The current format records each entry with an
explicit content-derived `event_id`. The older archive format used its own
`origin_ref` per entry and stored an export-observed `at` value rather than the
canonical recording time. It could renumber ids and restamp an event between
exports, so overlapping archive batches sometimes contain the same underlying
event twice with slightly different `at` values. Reading that format therefore
requires deciding when two archived entries are the same event and choosing one
representative timestamp deterministically.

`metadata` is caller-supplied descriptive context. It is never an input to an
entry's identity, and never an input to whether an entry is retained.

HTTP routing keeps request-path matching in `auditlog.paths` so
authentication and dispatch share one helper. V2 paths are aliases of
canonical V1 routes; resolving one through `auditlog.httpd` never yields a
weaker bearer requirement than its V1 route has. Client version selection
picks which path is called, never whether the call needs a bearer credential:
an alias with no declared requirement inherits the V1 route's (defaulting to
required if the V1 route is unknown), and an alias with an explicit
requirement is still floored by the V1 route, so a stale or mis-declared
catalog entry cannot open an unauthenticated path onto data V1 protects.

`record`, `query`, and `repair` are written only against the storage-independent
`LogStore` contract in `auditlog.service` (`read_only`, `load()`, `save()`), so a
new log-store format is added by writing one class that satisfies the
contract, not by teaching those functions a new branch. `SqliteLogStore` is
that proof: a brand-new `--log-store STORE.db` path becomes a durable SQLite
file, where every write commits as its own transaction, so a record made by
one process is durably visible to a query made by a separate process. The
JSON current and archive formats remain readable (and, for the archive,
migratable via `repair`) through the same `open_store` detection, based on
each file's own content, never its name.

`auditlog.httpd` also runs the one thing actually served over HTTP:
bearer-protected V1 routes (`POST /v1/entries`, `GET /v1/entries`, `GET
/v1/integrity`) backed by the same `LogStore` contract. `resolve_v1_route` is
the single lookup both the auth check and the dispatch use, so there is one
route decision, not two. The V2 alias catalog in `auditlog.policy` and its
resolution in `auditlog.httpd` are tested but not installed into that
server; nothing in the live route table references them. `auditlog.sdk_client`
is a small generated V1 client, one method per route, that always sends the
bearer credential those routes require.

`fixtures/sdk-request-response-fixtures.json` pins the exact request shape
(method, path, bearer header placement, body/query keys) and response shape
(exact key list, in order) for `record`, `query`, and `integrity`.
`tests/test_sdk_fixtures.py` checks the generated client against it two ways:
offline, by capturing the `Request` `AuditV1Client` builds without any network
call, and live, by running a real V1 server and checking response shape,
byte-for-byte JSON stability across repeated calls on unchanged state, and
that only the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header authenticates — a token
in the query string, the request body, or a header missing the `Bearer`
prefix is refused.

`auditlog.migration_diagnostics` compares the V1 calls the generated SDK
client actually issues against the planned V2 catalog (`auditlog.policy`)
entirely offline: `diagnose_migration` is pure data over data (no I/O), so
this comparison never sends V2 traffic — there is nothing to send it to, since
`create_server` never installs a V2 route. `capture_v1_calls` is the one
function that performs I/O, and it only drives the generated V1 client
against a live server to record what it actually sends; the recorded shape is
also pinned in `fixtures/v1-generated-calls.jsonl`. Runtime routing is
unchanged by any of this: the diagnostics module only reads
`auditlog.httpd.V1_ROUTES` and `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`, never installs
anything.

`auditlog.migration_reference` renders `docs/sdk-migration-reference.md`
from the compatibility catalog (`auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog`):
one Markdown row per stored catalog row, in the catalog's own order,
preserving each row's method, path, permission, and bearer requirement
exactly (an unset requirement is rendered as unset, never coerced to a
guessed boolean). A second row addressing a (method, path) pair already
seen is rejected rather than silently rendered. Rendering is pure and
offline — it never sends a request or touches what `auditlog.httpd`
serves — and rendering the same catalog twice always produces the same
text; `tests/test_migration_reference.py` checks the committed doc still
matches what the catalog renders today.

`auditlog.migration_checkpoint.CheckpointStore` gives a migration that
drives many generated-client calls a restart-safe record of progress: for
each call's own opaque `call_id` it persists only that id and a `pending`
or `completed` status, in a SQLite file where every write commits as its
own transaction — the same durability `SqliteLogStore` relies on, so a
completion one process marks is immediately visible to a separate process
opened against the same file. It never persists a call's payload, its
response, or the bearer credential used to make it.
`auditlog.migration_replay.replay` drives a list of `ReplayCall`s against
one of these stores: a call already marked complete is never invoked
again, and two calls in one batch can never share a `call_id` that
addresses different calls (`ReplayConflictError`). A call is marked
pending before it is invoked and complete only after, so a crash mid-call
leaves it pending — safe to retry, never falsely complete — for the next
replay, in a separate process if need be, to pick up. Because a V1
record's identity includes the timestamp the server stamps at receipt
(never the client's), a retried `record` call cannot be recognized as
"the same call" by content alone the way an unretried one can; a
`ReplayCall` may supply `already_applied` — a check the caller defines,
such as querying for the record — so a call that already succeeded just
before its checkpoint write was interrupted is marked complete without
being issued again rather than duplicated. None of this ever rewrites or
removes an existing audit record; `tests/test_migration_checkpoint.py`
and `tests/test_migration_replay.py` cover crash recovery, duplicate
replies, conflicting call ids, and continuation from a genuinely separate
OS process.

The project must remain local-only and use the Python standard library. Tests use
`unittest`, so the environment needs no dependency installation.

# Compliance Audit Log starter

A small, disposable starter for a local compliance audit-log service. The run
prompts grow it into a working service while preserving a stable CLI:

```text
python -m auditlog.cli record ACTOR ACTION OUTCOME --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli query --actor ACTOR --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli repair --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli serve --log-store STORE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --host HOST --port PORT
```

The trail is append-only. An entry, once recorded, is never removed, rewritten,
or reordered: corrections are made by recording a further entry, not by editing
history. Each entry carries a gapless `sequence` and an `event_id` derived
deterministically from the entry's own recorded content, so the same content
always yields the same id and any later edit is detectable by recomputing it.

Two log-store formats exist. The current format records each entry with an
explicit content-derived `event_id`. The older archive format used its own
`origin_ref` per entry and stored an export-observed `at` value rather than the
canonical recording time. It could renumber ids and restamp an event between
exports, so overlapping archive batches sometimes contain the same underlying
event twice with slightly different `at` values. Reading that format therefore
requires deciding when two archived entries are the same event and choosing one
representative timestamp deterministically.

`metadata` is caller-supplied descriptive context. It is never an input to an
entry's identity, and never an input to whether an entry is retained.

HTTP routing keeps request-path matching in `auditlog.paths` so
authentication and dispatch share one helper. V2 paths are aliases of
canonical V1 routes; resolving one through `auditlog.httpd` never yields a
weaker bearer requirement than its V1 route has. Client version selection
picks which path is called, never whether the call needs a bearer credential:
an alias with no declared requirement inherits the V1 route's (defaulting to
required if the V1 route is unknown), and an alias with an explicit
requirement is still floored by the V1 route, so a stale or mis-declared
catalog entry cannot open an unauthenticated path onto data V1 protects.

`record`, `query`, and `repair` are written only against the storage-independent
`LogStore` contract in `auditlog.service` (`read_only`, `load()`, `save()`), so a
new log-store format is added by writing one class that satisfies the
contract, not by teaching those functions a new branch. `SqliteLogStore` is
that proof: a brand-new `--log-store STORE.db` path becomes a durable SQLite
file, where every write commits as its own transaction, so a record made by
one process is durably visible to a query made by a separate process. The
JSON current and archive formats remain readable (and, for the archive,
migratable via `repair`) through the same `open_store` detection, based on
each file's own content, never its name.

`auditlog.httpd` runs what is actually served over HTTP: bearer-protected V1
routes (`POST /v1/entries`, `GET /v1/entries`, `GET /v1/integrity`) backed by
the same `LogStore` contract, plus their V2 aliases. `resolve_v1_route` is
the single lookup both the V1 auth check and dispatch use, and
`resolve_v2_route` is its V2 counterpart, so there is one route decision per
version, not two per request. `create_server` calls `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`
at startup against the turn-3 catalog (`auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog`)
and the live V1 bearer table, and installs the resolved aliases on the
server it builds: a V2 alias is reachable, and its bearer requirement can
only ever be at least as strict as its canonical V1 route's, never weaker. A
request matching neither a V1 route nor an installed V2 alias is still
unknown (404), exactly as before. `auditlog.sdk_client`'s `AuditV1Client`
takes an `api_version` (`"v1"` by default, or `"v2"`) that selects which
resolved path each call addresses without changing how the bearer credential
is sent — every call still sends the same `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
header regardless of version. `python -m auditlog.cli serve --log-store
STORE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --host HOST --port PORT` exposes this same
server; it opens `STORE.db` through the same `open_store` detection `query`
uses, so a `query` run afterward against the same `--log-store` path sees
what `serve` recorded.

`fixtures/sdk-request-response-fixtures.json` pins the exact request shape
(method, path, bearer header placement, body/query keys) and response shape
(exact key list, in order) for `record`, `query`, and `integrity`.
`tests/test_sdk_fixtures.py` checks the generated client against it two ways:
offline, by capturing the `Request` `AuditV1Client` builds without any network
call, and live, by running a real V1 server and checking response shape,
byte-for-byte JSON stability across repeated calls on unchanged state, and
that only the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header authenticates — a token
in the query string, the request body, or a header missing the `Bearer`
prefix is refused.

`auditlog.migration_diagnostics` compares the V1 calls the generated SDK
client actually issues against the planned V2 catalog (`auditlog.policy`)
entirely offline: `diagnose_migration` is pure data over data (no I/O), so
this comparison never sends V2 traffic — there is nothing to send it to, since
`create_server` never installs a V2 route. `capture_v1_calls` is the one
function that performs I/O, and it only drives the generated V1 client
against a live server to record what it actually sends; the recorded shape is
also pinned in `fixtures/v1-generated-calls.jsonl`. Runtime routing is
unchanged by any of this: the diagnostics module only reads
`auditlog.httpd.V1_ROUTES` and `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`, never installs
anything.

`auditlog.migration_reference` renders `docs/sdk-migration-reference.md`
from the compatibility catalog (`auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog`):
one Markdown row per stored catalog row, in the catalog's own order,
preserving each row's method, path, permission, and bearer requirement
exactly (an unset requirement is rendered as unset, never coerced to a
guessed boolean). A second row addressing a (method, path) pair already
seen is rejected rather than silently rendered. Rendering is pure and
offline — it never sends a request or touches what `auditlog.httpd`
serves — and rendering the same catalog twice always produces the same
text; `tests/test_migration_reference.py` checks the committed doc still
matches what the catalog renders today.

`auditlog.migration_checkpoint.CheckpointStore` gives a migration that
drives many generated-client calls a restart-safe record of progress: for
each call's own opaque `call_id` it persists only that id and a `pending`
or `completed` status, in a SQLite file where every write commits as its
own transaction — the same durability `SqliteLogStore` relies on, so a
completion one process marks is immediately visible to a separate process
opened against the same file. It never persists a call's payload, its
response, or the bearer credential used to make it.
`auditlog.migration_replay.replay` drives a list of `ReplayCall`s against
one of these stores: a call already marked complete is never invoked
again, and two calls in one batch can never share a `call_id` that
addresses different calls (`ReplayConflictError`). A call is marked
pending before it is invoked and complete only after, so a crash mid-call
leaves it pending — safe to retry, never falsely complete — for the next
replay, in a separate process if need be, to pick up. Because a V1
record's identity includes the timestamp the server stamps at receipt
(never the client's), a retried `record` call cannot be recognized as
"the same call" by content alone the way an unretried one can; a
`ReplayCall` may supply `already_applied` — a check the caller defines,
such as querying for the record — so a call that already succeeded just
before its checkpoint write was interrupted is marked complete without
being issued again rather than duplicated. None of this ever rewrites or
removes an existing audit record; `tests/test_migration_checkpoint.py`
and `tests/test_migration_replay.py` cover crash recovery, duplicate
replies, conflicting call ids, and continuation from a genuinely separate
OS process.

The project must remain local-only and use the Python standard library. Tests use
`unittest`, so the environment needs no dependency installation.
